sub_documents.title: Asset Toolkit
sub_documents.summary: The Asset Toolkit in Kanzi Studio provides ready-made components and materials to accelerate application development. It includes a placeholder car model, PBR materials (carpaint, chrome, glass, plastic), environment textures for ambient and specular lighting, Flipbook and Transition material types for animated content, interactive UI components (buttons, etc.) with shared properties, radial UI components for circular progress, simple shape components, scroll list components in four layout patterns, and example components. Assets are used by dragging from Asset Packages into the project. The page details how to configure each asset type, such as setting grid and static image index for Flipbook, transition type and progress for Transition materials, and various UI properties like fill, stroke, segments, and progress.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Asset Toolkit[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#asset-toolkit "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
The Asset Toolkit contains easy, ready-made components and materials with a similar structure and set of properties, that you can use to create Kanzi applications faster.
Here you can find all the Asset Toolkit content:
  * A high quality placeholder car model that you can use in your prototype application. See [Car](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#car).
  * Materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project. See [Materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#materials).
  * Environment Textures that you can use to give perspective to your scene. See [Environments](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#environments).
  * Flipbook and Transition Material types that you can use to present content in your application. See [Material types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#material-types).
  * Interactive User Interface Components that you can use to receive user input. See [Interactivity Control components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#interactivity-control-components).
  * Radial UI Components that you can show progress in a circular arc. See [Radial UI Components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#radial-ui-components).
  * Simple shapes to use in your application. See [Simple Shape UI Components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#simple-shape-ui-components).
  * Scrollable lists that can present collections of items. See [Scroll list UI Components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#scroll-list-ui-components).
  * Example components that shows ways to combine these assets into more complex, reusable components. See [Examples](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#examples).


To use the Asset Toolkit assets in your Kanzi Studio project, from the Asset Packages drag an asset to a node in the Node Tree, to the Prefabs, or to the Preview. See [Using the Asset Toolkit assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html).
![../../_images/asset-packages-asset-toolkit-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-asset-toolkit-selected.png)
## Car[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#car "Link to this heading")
Use the Car to add a car model into your scene.
![../../_images/car-asset1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-asset1.png)
To position the car, in the Preview use either the Node tool or the Camera tool. See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html) and [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).
To set the material for the different parts of the car, you can drag materials from the Assets window to the Car in the Preview window, or on the part of the car in the Node Tree. See [Using the Asset Toolkit assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html).
## Materials[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#materials "Link to this heading")
The Asset Toolkit includes Physically Based Rendering (PBR) materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project.
![../../_images/carpaint-blue.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carpaint-blue.png)
PBR Carpaint-blue
![../../_images/carpaint-orange.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carpaint-orange.png)
PBR Carpaint-orange
![../../_images/chrome.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/chrome.png)
PBR Chrome
![../../_images/glass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/glass.png)
PBR Glass
![../../_images/plastic.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/plastic.png)
PBR Plastic
To learn about using materials from the Asset Toolkit in your Kanzi application, see [Using Asset Toolkit materials in your project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html#using-at-materials).
## Environments[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#environments "Link to this heading")
The Asset Toolkit includes two environment textures which are also included in the car and PBR materials, but provided independently for use with your own materials or models.
  * Use Environment Studio Irradiance to provide diffused ambient lighting to materials in your scene, as is done with glass and plastics in the assets.


![../../_images/environment-irradiance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-irradiance.png)
Environment Studio Irradiance
  * Use Environment Studio Specular to provide a sharp, smooth reflective surface to materials in your scene, as is done with metals and paint in the assets.


![../../_images/environment-specular.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-specular.png)
Environment Studio Specular
To use an environment texture in your project, from the Assets window right-click and import, and apply to your materials by setting it as the Ambient and/or Reflection texture in the material properties. Control its strength by adjusting the Factor slider.
![../../_images/set-environment-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-environment-texture.png)
To learn more about environment textures, see [Using environment textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html).
## Material types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#material-types "Link to this heading")
The Asset Toolkit includes two Material Types that can be used to animate display of content in your application:
  * The Flipbook Material Type allows you to use a texture atlas that contains multiple images arranged in a grid layout. Use it to selectively display images from that texture atlas, or to play out an animated sequence. This is useful for example, to set the state of navigation arrow in a cluster, or to animate a simple pedestrian figure walking.
![../../_images/flipbook.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flipbook.png)
Flipbook Material Type
To use the Flipbook Material Type in your project:
    * Right-click to import or drag it into your preview or node tree.
    * Apply it as a brush to 2D or 3D nodes in your scene.
    * In the Flipbook Material Type properties window, set the grid to correspond to the layout of the images in the texture atlas.
![../../_images/flipbook-configuration.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flipbook-configuration.png)
    * Set the static image to display by setting the Static Image Index property.
![../../_images/static-image-index.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/static-image-index.png)
    * Play out an animated flipbook sequence by advancing the Time property value.
![../../_images/time-sequence.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/time-sequence.png)
To learn about using tile atlases, see [Using a tile atlas](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-tile-atlases.html).
  * The Transition Material Type allows you to transition between nodes in either a Fade, Sweep or Noise motion.
![../../_images/transition.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/transition.png)
Transition Material Type
To use the Transition Material Type in your project:
    * Right-click to import or drag it into your preview or node tree.
    * Apply it as a brush to 2D or 3D nodes in your scene.
    * In the Transition Material Type properties window,
      * Set the Transition Type to apply to the transition.
      * Select textures between which to transition as the Transition Texture Start and Transition Texture End properties.
![../../_images/transition-textures.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/transition-textures.png)
    * To apply a Fade transition, set the Transition type property to Fade.
      * Control the progression of the fade by advancing the Transition Progress property value.
![../../_images/fade-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fade-properties.png)
    * To apply a Sweep transition, set the Transition type property to Sweep.
      * Control the smoothing intensity by setting the Transition Smoothing property
      * Set orientation of the sweep motion using the Transition Rotation property.
![../../_images/sweep-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sweep-properties.png)
    * To apply a Noise transition, set the Transition type property to Noise.
      * Additionally, control the granularity of the noise by setting the Transition Noise Scale property.
![../../_images/noise-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/noise-properties.png)


## Interactivity Control components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#interactivity-control-components "Link to this heading")
Use the UI Components provided in the Asset Toolkit to receive user input, and provide an interactive user experience in your application.
![../../_images/interactivity-ui-components.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interactivity-ui-components.png)
The interactive UI components included in the Asset Toolkit all share a set of similar properties and behaviors, exposed and named the same way. This makes it easier to apply consistent styling, and to combine them in your project.
When you import a UI component, Kanzi Studio adds to your project Library and Prefabs, the required shaders and materials to render that component.
It uses the FillStrokeBrush material, applied as BackgroundBrush to all the UI components, to expose properties that control their appearance and behavior.
![../../_images/fillstrokebrush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fillstrokebrush.png) ![../../_images/fillstrokebrush-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fillstrokebrush-properties.png)
For example, to adjust the appearance and behavior of the Button, after you add the Button to your project, in the Properties set:
  * UI - Appearance to set the Corner Radius value that adjust the roundness of the button corners.
  * UI - Fill to set the Fill Color of the button background.
  * UI - Fill Gradient to set the Fill Gradient Color of the button background and its Rotation.
  * UI - Fill Texture to apply a texture to the button background and set how it should be applied.
  * UI - Progress to apply a progress bar state across the background of the button.
  * UI - Segments to divide the button background into segments, and set its number and weight.
  * UI - Stroke to apply an outline to the button, and set its color and weight.


Use any combination of these properties to adjust the appearance of the UI components. Each are enabled individually by marking the property Active.
![../../_images/fill-gradient-active.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fill-gradient-active.png)
You can use bindings to control the UI - Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
To learn more about the interactivity controls, see [Interactivity controls](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/controls/controls.html).
## Radial UI Components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#radial-ui-components "Link to this heading")
Use the Radial UI Components provided in the Asset Toolkit display values to progress in a round control.
![../../_images/radial-components.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/radial-components.png)
The Radial UI components included in the Asset Toolkit all share a set of similar properties and behaviors, exposed and named the same way.
When you import a UI component, Kanzi Studio adds to your project Library and Prefabs, the required shaders and materials to render that component.
It uses the FillStrokeRadialBrush material, applied as BackgroundBrush to all the UI components, to expose properties that control their appearance and behavior.
![../../_images/fillstrokeradialbrush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fillstrokeradialbrush.png) ![../../_images/fillstrokeradialbrush-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fillstrokeradialbrush-properties.png)
For example, to adjust the appearance and behavior of the Gauge Progress control, after you add it to your project, in the Properties set:
  * UI - Appearance to set the angle at which to apply progress, its radial weight and cap shape.
  * UI - Fill to set the Fill Color of the UI background.
  * UI - Progress to apply progression state across the background of the dial, and its color.
  * UI - Segments to divide the gauge into segments, and set its number and weight.
  * UI - Stroke to apply an outline to the gauge, and set its color and weight.


Use any combination of these properties to adjust the appearance of the Radial UI components. Each are enabled individually by marking the property Active.
![../../_images/segments-active.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/segments-active.png)
You can use bindings to control the UI - Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
## Simple Shape UI Components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#simple-shape-ui-components "Link to this heading")
Use the simple shape UI components provided in the Asset Toolkit to add basic shapes to your application without the need of a plugin.
![../../_images/simple-shapes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/simple-shapes.png)
  * On the Box with Rounded Corners, set the Corner Radius property to square or round out the shape.
  * On the Circle, set the UI - Fill property values to apply color.


## Scroll list UI Components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#scroll-list-ui-components "Link to this heading")
Use the scroll list UI components provided in the Asset Toolkit to add scrollable lists to your application in one of a four layout patterns.
![../../_images/scroll-list-ui-components.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/scroll-list-ui-components.png)
  * Use the Scroll List Vertical to present items two dimensionally in a vertical scrollable list.
  * Use the Horizontal List Vertical to present items two dimensionally in a horizontally scrollable list.
  * Use the Scroll Trajectory 3D Horizontal to present the items three dimensionally in on horizontal plane.
  * Use the Scroll Trajectory 3D Arc to present the items three dimensionally in an arc.


To learn more about list, see [List Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html).
To use a data source to display your own data in a list component, see [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html), and [Tutorial: Get application data from a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-sources/data-sources.html).
## Examples[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#examples "Link to this heading")
Expand the Asset Toolkit to find a folder with example components that show possible ways to combine these assets into more complex, reusable components.
![../../_images/examples.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/examples.png)
Explore these example components for practical ideas on assembling your own custom controls by combining them.
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Using the Asset Toolkit assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html)

[3D assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/3d-assets/3d-assets.html)
[Material types and materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/materials.html)
[Tutorial: Materials and textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/materials-and-textures/materials-and-textures.html)
[Using node prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html)

sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Automating Kanzi Studio tasks[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#automating-ks-tasks "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
You can execute Kanzi Studio commands by running a script from the command line interface. This enables you to automate repetitive tasks in Kanzi Studio or Kanzi Studio tasks that you must execute on a large number of Kanzi Studio projects. For example, consider making a script to update a Kanzi Engine plugin that you use in many Kanzi Studio projects, or to export kzb files from many Kanzi Studio projects.
For the list of available commands, see [Kanzi Studio command reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html).
To automate Kanzi Studio tasks:
  1. In a text editor, create a script where you define what commands you want Kanzi Studio to run.
For example, add to the script the commands in this step and save the script as `MyScript.txt`.
    1. Open a Kanzi Studio project.

```
# Open the project named MyProject.
LoadProject "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyProject\Tool_project\MyProject.proj.kzm"

```
Copy to clipboard
    2. Add commands to automate Kanzi Studio tasks.
For example, you can automate:
       * Exporting of kzb files. See [Exporting kzb files using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#exporting-kzb-files-using-a-script).
       * Building of Kanzi applications for Android. See [Building Kanzi applications for Android using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#building-kanzi-applications-for-android-using-script).
       * Importing and updating of Kanzi Engine plugins. See [Importing and updating Kanzi Engine plugins using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#importing-and-updating-kanzi-engine-plugins-using-script).
       * Creating and updating of data sources. See [Creating and updating data sources using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-and-updating-data-sources-using-a-script).
       * Creating of nodes. See [Creating nodes using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-nodes-using-a-script).
       * Adding and removing of properties, and setting of property values. See [Editing properties using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#editing-properties-using-a-script).
       * Logging of invalid project items. See [Logging invalid project items using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#logging-invalid-project-items-using-a-script).
For the list of available commands, see [Kanzi Studio command reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html).
    3. Save and close the project.

```
# Save the project.
# The second parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio continues working in the directory where you
# opened the project.
# When you save the project to a different location, set the second parameter to false.
# For example,
# SaveProject "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyOtherProject\Tool_project\MyOtherProject.proj.kzm" false
SaveProject "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyProject\Tool_project\MyProject.proj.kzm" true

# Close Kanzi Studio.
# To close the project but continue using Kanzi Studio, use CloseProject.
ExitApplication

```
Copy to clipboard
  2. Open the command line interface, go to the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin` directory, and run the `KanziStudio.exe` file with the `/Script` flag pointing to the script that you created in the previous step.
For example, on the command line interface, run

```
KanziStudio.exe /Script="C:\Users\username\Documents\MyScript.txt"

```
Copy to clipboard


## Exporting kzb files using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#exporting-kzb-files-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
A kzb file contains contents of a Kanzi Studio project. To run your Kanzi application, you must export the contents of the Kanzi Studio project of that application to a kzb file.
See [Using kzb files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/using-kzb-binaries.html).
To export kzb files using a script, use the [ExportBinary](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#exportbinary) command:

```
# Export the kzb file to the location set in the Project > Properties in the Binary Export Directory
# property.
# To export the kzb file to another location use:
# ExportBinary "Path\to\directory\MyProjectBinary.kzb"
ExportBinary

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/binary-export-directory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binary-export-directory.png) ![../../_images/export-kzb-binary.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-kzb-binary.png)
The `ExportBinary` command takes these optional parameters:
  * The first parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio exports the theme and locale resources to separate kzb files. The default is true.
  * The second parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio exports kza file, which is the XML version of the kzb file. The default is false.


For example, to export both the theme and locale resources to separate kzb files, and the kza file:

```
# Export the theme and locale resources and the kza file.
ExportBinary true true

```
Copy to clipboard
## Building Kanzi applications for Android using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#building-k-applications-for-android-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
To build Kanzi applications for Android using a script, use the [ExportApk](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#exportapk) command:

```
# Before you build an APK file, you can set whether to install the APK file to your
# Android device and launch the application. By default, |k| installs the APK file
# and launches the application.
# In My Android Configuration, disable the Install to Device property.
SetProperty "/Resource Files/Build Configurations/My Android Configuration" BuildConfigurationInstallToDevice false
# In My Android Configuration, disable the Launch Application property.
SetProperty "/Resource Files/Build Configurations/My Android Configuration" BuildConfigurationRunApplication false

# Build the APK file using the My Android Configuration build configuration.
# If the project contains images that use texture compression, the second
# parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio compresses these images.
ExportApk "/Resource Files/Build Configurations/My Android Configuration" true

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/library-my-android-configuration.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-my-android-configuration.png) ![../../_images/properties-my-android-configuration.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-my-android-configuration.png) ![../../_images/build-android-package.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/build-android-package.png)
## Importing and updating Kanzi Engine plugins using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#importing-and-updating-kr-plugins-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Engine plugins extend the functionality of Kanzi Engine. Kanzi Engine executes these plugins on target platforms.
See [Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/plugins-kanzi-engine.html).
You can import and update Kanzi Engine plugins using a script:
  * [Importing a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#importing-kanzi-engine-plugin-using-script)
  * [Updating a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-kanzi-engine-plugin-using-script)
  * [Updating all Kanzi Engine plugins in a project or solution using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-all-kanzi-engine-plugins-in-project-or-solution-using-script)


### Importing a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#importing-a-kr-plugin-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
When you want to use a Kanzi Engine plugin in a Kanzi Studio project, you must import that Kanzi Engine plugin to your Kanzi Studio project.
To import a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script, use the [ImportEnginePlugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#importengineplugin) command:

```
# Import the Kanzi Engine plugin DLL MyPluginProject\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Debug_DLL\MyPluginProject.dll.
# Kanzi Studio adds to the Library > Kanzi Engine Plugins a reference to the Kanzi Engine plugin DLL that you import.
ImportEnginePlugin "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyPluginProject\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Debug_DLL\MyPluginProject.dll"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/import-kanzi-engine-plugin.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/import-kanzi-engine-plugin.png) ![../../_images/mypluginproject-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mypluginproject-in-library.png)
### Updating a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-a-kr-plugin-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
When you want to use in a Kanzi Studio project a different version of a Kanzi Engine plugin, you must update that Kanzi Engine plugin in your Kanzi Studio project.
To update a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script, use the [ImportEnginePlugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#importengineplugin) command:

```
# Update the XML_data_source Kanzi Engine plugin in the project.
# You leave the first parameter empty because you do not import a new plugin to the project.
ImportEnginePlugin "" "/Kanzi Engine Plugins/XML_data_source"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/update-kanzi-engine-plugin-metadata.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/update-kanzi-engine-plugin-metadata.png)
### Updating all Kanzi Engine plugins in a project or solution using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-all-kr-plugins-in-a-project-or-solution-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
When you want to use in a Kanzi Studio project a different version of a Kanzi Engine plugin, you must update that Kanzi Engine plugin in your Kanzi Studio project.
You can update all Kanzi Engine plugins in your Kanzi Studio project using a script. If your Kanzi Studio project contains project references, you can update all Kanzi Engine plugins in the solution which includes that project and all referenced projects. See [Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html).
To update all Kanzi Engine plugins in a project or solution using a script, use the [UpdateProjectEnginePlugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updateprojectengineplugins) or [UpdateSolutionEnginePlugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updatesolutionengineplugins) command:

```
# Update all the Kanzi Engine plugins in the project.
# To update the Kanzi Engine plugins in that project and all referenced projects use
# UpdateSolutionEnginePlugins.
UpdateProjectEnginePlugins

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/update-kanzi-engine-plugins-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/update-kanzi-engine-plugins-in-project.png)
## Creating and updating data sources using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-and-updating-data-sources-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
Use data sources to separate the user interface from the application data and to remove the dependencies between a Kanzi Studio project and the application code which define the Kanzi application.
See [Data sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/data-sources.html).
You can create and update data sources using a script:
  * [Creating a data source using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-a-data-source-using-a-script)
  * [Updating a data source using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-a-data-source-using-a-script)
  * [Updating all data sources in a project or solution using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-all-data-sources-in-a-project-or-solution-using-a-script)


### Creating a data source using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-a-data-source-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
When you want to use a Kanzi Engine data source plugin in a Kanzi Studio project, you must create a data source in your Kanzi Studio project.
To create a data source using a script, first import a Kanzi Engine data source plugin, then create and update the data source:

```
# Import the Kanzi Engine data source plugin DLL MyDataSource\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Release_DLL\MyDataSource.dll.
# The MyDataSource plugin defines the CustomDataSourceType data source type.
# Kanzi Studio adds to the Library > Kanzi Engine Plugins a reference to the Kanzi Engine data source plugin DLL that you import.
ImportEnginePlugin "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyDataSource\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Release_DLL\MyDataSource.dll"

# Create a data source named Cluster of the type CustomDataSourceType.
CreateDataSource "Cluster" "CustomDataSourceType"
# To create data objects from the Cluster data source, update the data source.
UpdateDataSourceContents "/Data Sources/Cluster/"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/mydatasource-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mydatasource-in-library.png) ![../../_images/mydatasource-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mydatasource-properties.png) ![../../_images/cluster-data-source.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cluster-data-source.png)
### Updating a data source using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-a-data-source-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
If the Kanzi Engine plugin that defines your data source does not update your data source, you can update the data source using a script.
To update a data source using a script, use the [UpdateDataSourceContents](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updatedatasourcecontents) command:

```
# Update the Cluster data source in the project.
UpdateDataSourceContents "/Data Sources/Cluster/"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/update-data-source.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/update-data-source.png)
### Updating all data sources in a project or solution using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-all-data-sources-in-a-project-or-solution-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
If the Kanzi Engine plugin that defines your data source does not update your data sources, you can update the data source using a script. If your Kanzi Studio project contains project references, you can update all data sources in the solution which includes that project and all referenced projects. See [Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html).
To update all data sources in a project or solution using a script, use the [UpdateProjectDataSources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updateprojectdatasources) or [UpdateSolutionDataSources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updatesolutiondatasources) command:

```
# Update all data sources in the project.
# To update the data sources in that project and all referenced projects use
# UpdateSolutionDataSources.
UpdateProjectDataSources

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/update-data-sources-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/update-data-sources-in-project.png)
## Creating nodes using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-nodes-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
You can create nodes using a script. For example:
  * To create a Button 2D node, use the [CreateButton2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#createbutton2d) command:

```
# In the RootNode node, create a Button 2D node named My Button.
# The last parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio selects the node that you created.
CreateButton2D "/Screens/Screen/RootNode" "My Button" true

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/my-button-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-button-in-project.png)
  * To create a Grid List Box 3D node, use the [CreateComponentNode](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#createcomponentnode) command:

```
# In the RootNode > Viewport 2D > Scene node, create a Grid List Box 3D node named My Grid List Box.
CreateComponentNode "/Screens/Screen/RootNode/Viewport 2D/Scene" "My Grid List Box" Kanzi.GridListBox3D

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/my-grid-list-box-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-grid-list-box-in-project.png)


## Editing properties using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#editing-properties-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
Properties provide the means to specify and examine the state, appearance, and behavior of nodes. For example, a property can define a color, indicate whether a button is pressed, or specify the alignment of an item.
See [Property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/property-types.html).
You can edit properties using a script:
  * [Adding properties using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#adding-properties-using-a-script)
  * [Removing properties using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#removing-properties-using-a-script)
  * [Setting property values using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#setting-property-values-using-a-script)


### Adding properties using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#adding-properties-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
To add properties using a script, use the [AddProperty](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#addproperty) command.
For example, to add the Description property to the RootNode node:

```
# In the RootNode node, add the Description property.
AddProperty "MyProject/Screens/Screen/RootNode" Description

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/rootpage-description.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rootpage-description.png)
### Removing properties using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#removing-properties-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
To remove properties using a script, use the [RemovePropertyFromItem](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#removepropertyfromitem) command.
For example, to remove the Background Brush property from the RootNode node:

```
# In the RootNode node, remove the Background Brush property.
# Use the Kanzi Engine property name which you see in Kanzi Studio when you hover your
# mouse pointer over the property name.
RemovePropertyFromItem "MyProject/Screens/Screen/RootNode" Node2D.BackgroundBrush

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/background-brush-kanzi-engine-name.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-brush-kanzi-engine-name.png) ![../../_images/remove-background-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/remove-background-brush.png)
### Setting property values using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#setting-property-values-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
To set property values using a script, use the [SetProperty](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#setproperty) command.
For example:
  * To set the size of the Screen node to 1200 x 720 pixels:

```
# In the Screen node, set:
# - Metrics Type to Absolute
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen" Window.MetricsType Absolute
# - Width to 1200
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen" WindowAbsoluteWidth 1200
# - Height to 720
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen" WindowAbsoluteHeight 720

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/metrics-type-absolute.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/metrics-type-absolute.png) ![../../_images/window-width-and-height-1200x720.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/window-width-and-height-1200x720.png)
  * To set the Text property of a Text Block node to one line of text:

```
# In the RootNode > My Text Block node, set the Text property to SERVICE VEHICLE SOON.
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen/RootNode/My Text Block" TextConcept.Text "SERVICE VEHICLE SOON"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/text-single-line.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-single-line.png)
  * To set a property value that spans multiple lines, enclose the value between triple backticks:

```
# In the RootNode > My Text Block node, set the Text property to
# SERVICE
# VEHICLE
# SOON
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen/RootNode/My Text Block" TextConcept.Text ```SERVICE
VEHICLE
SOON```

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/text-multiline.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-multiline.png)


## Logging invalid project items using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#logging-invalid-project-items-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Studio marks invalid items in the Node Tree and Library with red type.
For example:
  * A node contains an invalid binding.
  * A resource uses a resource that does not exist or is missing a required property.
  * A material type has precision mismatches in its shaders.
  * A shader source file contains errors.

![../../_images/node-with-invalid-binding-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-with-invalid-binding-in-project.png)
See [Finding invalid project items](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/finding-invalid-project-items.html).
To log invalid project items in your Kanzi Studio project using a script, use the [PrintDiagnosticReport](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#printdiagnosticreport) command:

```
# Print a list of invalid project items to the Log window and the KanziStudio.log file.
PrintDiagnosticReport MyProject

```
Copy to clipboard

sub_documents.title: Bindings
sub_documents.summary: This page from the Kanzi framework documentation provides an overview of bindings, which are used to set property values based on other properties or data sources. It explains the components of a binding (target item, target property, source), binding modes (one-way, to-source, two-way), binding types (value source, modifier, to-source), and material type bindings (uniform and temporary variable). It also includes examples and links to related tutorials and references.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#bindings "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use bindings to set the value of a property or property field with the value from another property, property field, or a data source.
Bindings allow nodes, render passes, 2D effects, states, state objects, and styles to automatically update the values of their properties in response to the changing property values, or the occurrence of some external event.
For example, you can:  
| Bind the rotation property field of a node to a property to create a gauge needle that you can control with that property. See [Tutorial: Create gauges](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/gauges/gauges.html).  |  ![../../_images/binding-rotation.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-rotation.png)  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Bind the position or size of one node to the position or size of another node. See [Tutorial: Making applications with dynamic layout](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/dynamic-layout/dynamic-layout.html).  |  ![../../_images/binding-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-size.png)  |  
With bindings you can modularize your Kanzi project:
  * Use bindings in prefabs to provide access only to those properties that you want to set to different values in different instances of the prefab. See [Customizing instances of a node prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-a-node-prefab).
  * Use bindings with data sources to separate the presentation of the user interface from the application data and to remove the dependencies between a Kanzi Studio project and the application code which defines the Kanzi application. This way you can build your Kanzi application according to the [Model-View-Controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model%E2%80%93view%E2%80%93controller) pattern. See [Data sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/data-sources.html).
For example, you can bind the presentation of a speed needle in the user interface to the data value which represents speed in your application. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html).


The simplest of bindings bind a property of a node to one of its own properties. You can also bind properties and property fields of one node to those of several different nodes. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
## Components of a binding[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#components-of-a-binding "Link to this heading")
A binding has these components:
  * Target item, which can be a node, render pass, 2D effect, state, state object, or style.
  * Target property and, optionally, property field.
  * Source returned by a binding expression.

![../../_images/components-of-a-binding.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/components-of-a-binding.svg)
The source can be a property or property field of a node, render pass, 2D effect, state, state object, style, or data object.
For example, to use a text block to show the current value of a slider, you can bind the Text (`TextConcept.Text`) property of a Text Block node to the Value property of a Slider node. The Text Block node is the target item, Text is the target property, and the Value (`RangeConcept.Value`) property of the Slider node is the source. See [Tutorial: Creating a slider](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/slider/slider.html).
![../../_images/binding-example.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-example.svg)
## Binding modes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#binding-modes "Link to this heading")
Binding mode sets the direction of data flow in the binding:
  * One way binding changes the value of a target property when the value of a source property changes.
In a one-way binding, you can bind the target property to a binding expression. See [Bindings expressions reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html).
![../../_images/binding-modes-one-way.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-modes-one-way.svg)
Note
When you use a state manager, action, or a style to set a local property value, that removes any one-way binding that targets the property. See [Value source bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#value-source-bindings).
  * To Source binding sets:
    * A property value in the project item that you set as the Push Target of the binding.
    * A property value that is affected also by some other source, such as user input. See [Creating a to-source binding](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#creating-a-to-source-binding).
    * A property value in a resource used by the item to which you add the binding.
For example, you can set a property value in a render pass or 2D effect instance used by a node. See [Customizing instances of a render pass prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings-to-customize-prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-a-render-pass-prefab) and [Customizing instances of a 2D effect prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings-to-customize-prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-a-2d-effect-prefab).
In a to-source binding, you can bind the target property to a binding expression. See [Bindings expressions reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html).
![../../_images/binding-modes-to-source.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-modes-to-source.svg)
  * Two way binding changes the value of a target property when the value of a source property changes, and the other way around.
In a two-way binding, you can bind a target property only to a source property. See [Creating a two-way binding](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#creating-a-two-way-binding).
![../../_images/binding-modes-two-way.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-modes-two-way.svg)


## Binding types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#binding-types "Link to this heading")
These types of bindings are available in Kanzi:
  * Value Sources
A value source binding sets the local value of an entire property and provides the value for that property during application runtime.
See [Value source bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#value-source-bindings).
  * Modifiers
A modifier binding modifies a property value, much like an animation or a state manager.
See [Modifier bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#modifier-bindings).
  * To Source
A to-source binding pushes a property value to a node or another project item, or to a resource used by that item.
See [To-source bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#to-source-bindings).

![../../_images/properties-binding-types.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-binding-types.png)
### Value source bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#value-source-bindings "Link to this heading")
A value source binding sets the local value of an entire property and provides the value for that property during application runtime.
For example, bind the Layout Height property of a 2D node to the Layout Width property of that node, or bind the Text property of a Text Block 2D node to the position of another node. See [Creating simple bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#creating-simple-bindings) and [Binding to the properties of other nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#binding-to-the-properties-of-other-nodes).
A value source binding replaces any previously set local property value.
Kanzi removes a value source binding when:
  * Setting the property value by other means replaces the previously set local value.
  * The local property value is removed.


For example:
  * A one-way value source binding that sets the Text property of a Tex Box node stops working when the user edits the text. To update the text with a binding, use a to-source or two-way binding instead. See [Using a binding to update the text in a Text Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#text-box-text-binding).
  * A one-way binding that sets the Toggle State property of a Toggle Button node stops working when the user toggles the button. To update the property value with a binding, use a to-source or two-way binding. See [Using a binding to update the toggle state](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#using-a-binding-to-update-the-toggle-state).


### Modifier bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#modifier-bindings "Link to this heading")
A modifier binding modifies a property value, much like an animation or a state manager.
A modifier binding either:
  * Sets the value of a property field.
For example, bind the Layout Transformation property Rotation property field of a node to the Scroll Position property of a Scroll View node to rotate the node using swiping gestures. See [Tutorial: Rotate a 3D model](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/rotation/rotation.html).
  * Accesses a value source in a binding expression.
For example, bind the Render Transformation property Translation Y property field of a node to the Render Transformation property Translation X property field of the same node to make that node move on the y axis the same distance as it moves on the x axis. See [Modifying the value of the property that you bind](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#modifying-the-value-of-the-property-that-you-bind) and [getCurrentValue](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#getcurrentvalue).


Kanzi executes modifier bindings after value Sources bindings. A modifier binding does not replace a local property value.
### To-source bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#to-source-bindings "Link to this heading")
A to-source binding pushes a property value to a node or another project item, or to a resource used by that item.
For example, use a to-source binding to:
  * Set a property value that is affected also by some other input source, such as user input.
For example:
    * In a List Box node, the Selected Item Index property.
    * In a Scroll View or Grid List Box node, the Scroll Position property.
    * In a Slider node, the Value property. [Updating the slider value with a property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/sliders/using-sliders.html#updating-the-slider-value-with-a-property).
    * In a Text Box node, the Text property. [Using a binding to update the text in a Text Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#text-box-text-binding).
    * In a Toggle Button node, the Toggle State property. See [Using a binding to update the toggle state](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html#using-a-binding-to-update-the-toggle-state).
    * In a Toggle Button Group node, the Current Button Index property.
  * Set a property value in a render pass prefab instance used by a Viewport 2D node. See [Customizing instances of a render pass prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings-to-customize-prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-a-render-pass-prefab).
  * Set a property value in an effect instance used by a 2D node. See [Customizing instances of a 2D effect prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings-to-customize-prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-a-2d-effect-prefab).


## Material type bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#material-type-bindings "Link to this heading")
Material types have their own special types of bindings for:
  * Uniforms
Uniform bindings enable you to modify the values of shader uniforms used by a material type without making changes to the shader code.
See [Uniform bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/materials.html#uniform-bindings).
  * Temporary Variables
In a material type, a temporary variable binding enables you to store the result of a binding into a temporary variable. You can refer to this variable in other bindings in the same material type.
See [Temporary variable bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/materials.html#temporary-variable-bindings).


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#sa "Link to this heading")

[Tutorial: Creating a slider](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/slider/slider.html)

sub_documents.title: Using bookmarks
sub_documents.summary: This page explains how to use bookmarks in Kanzi Studio to quickly access objects and resources. It covers creating bookmarks from any item via Alt+right-click, accessing bookmarked items by double-clicking in the Library, changing a bookmark's target via the Target property, and mentions bookmark property types. It also notes that aliases can be used for accessing nodes and that kzb file URLs are used in code.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Using bookmarks[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#using-bookmarks "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use bookmarks to provide a quick way to access objects and resources in your Kanzi Studio project. To access resources and objects in your Kanzi application in code, use the kzb file URL.
Kanzi Studio stores bookmarks in the Library > Bookmarks.
To access nodes in your Kanzi Studio project or using the Kanzi API you can also use aliases. See [Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html).
## Creating a bookmark from any item[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#creating-a-bookmark-from-any-item "Link to this heading")
To create a bookmark from any item in Kanzi Studio, in the Node Tree, Nodes, or Library press `Alt` and right-click and select Bookmark.
Kanzi Studio creates a bookmark and sets its Target property to the item from which you created the bookmark.
## Accessing a bookmarked item[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#accessing-a-bookmarked-item "Link to this heading")
To access a bookmarked item, in the Library > Bookmarks double-click the bookmark of the item you want to access.
Kanzi Studio takes you to the bookmarked item.
## Changing the target of a bookmark[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#changing-the-target-of-a-bookmark "Link to this heading")
To change the item to which a bookmark points, in the Library select the bookmark, and in the Properties set the Target property to the item you want the bookmark to point to.
##  Bookmark property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#bookmark-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for bookmarks, see [Bookmark](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/bookmark-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html)

sub_documents.title: Using brushes
sub_documents.summary: This page from the Kanzi documentation explains how to use brushes to define the appearance of 2D content. It covers the three types of brushes (Color, Texture, and Material), how to fill 2D nodes with solid colors, textures, or materials, how to set text color, control brush appearance in different states using state managers, and apply custom rendering effects like grayscale conversion using material brushes and shaders. It also mentions using brushes in the API and lists brush property types.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Using brushes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#using-brushes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Brushes are graphics objects that describe how 2D content is drawn.
Use Brushes to set the appearance of the foreground and background of 2D nodes. For example, with brushes you can define the color of text in a Text Block 2D node, fill a background of a 2D node with an image pattern, or apply a material effect on 2D content.
Most 2D nodes have a foreground and a background. With brushes you can change the appearance of both.
These brushes are available in Kanzi:
  * Color Brush to fill a 2D node with a solid color.
See [Filling 2D nodes with a solid color](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-solid-color).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png)
  * Texture Brush to fill a 2D node with a texture.
See [Filling 2D nodes with a texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-texture).
![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png)
  * Material Brush to fill a 2D node with a material.
See [Filling 2D nodes with a material](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-material).
![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)


Kanzi Studio stores brushes in the Library > Materials and Textures > Brushes.
![../../_images/brushes-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/brushes-in-library.png)
For example, with the brushes you can:
  * Set the color of 2D text. See [Setting the color of text in 2D text nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#setting-the-color-of-text-in-2d-text-nodes).
![../../_images/text.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text.png)
  * Define the appearance of brushes in different application states. See [Controlling the appearance of brushes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#controlling-the-appearance-of-brushes).
![../../_images/brush-appearance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/brush-appearance.png)
  * Create post-processing effects for 2D nodes. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#applying-custom-rendering-to-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)


## Filling 2D nodes with a solid color[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-solid-color "Link to this heading")
Use a Color Brush to fill a 2D node with a solid color.
To fill a 2D node with a solid color:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures, select Color Brush, and name the brush.
![../../_images/library-create-color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-create-color-brush.png) ![../../_images/dark-gray-color-brush-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dark-gray-color-brush-in-library.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select the 2D node that you want to fill with the brush you created, in the Properties add the Background Brush or the Foreground Brush property, and select the brush you created in the first step.
For example, create a Button 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to the brush you created in the first step.
![../../_images/button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-background-brush-set-to-dark-gray.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-background-brush-set-to-dark-gray.png)
  3. In the Properties click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) next to the property you added in the previous step and set the color of the color brush you created in the previous step.
In the Preview you can see that the Color Brush you created fills the node for which you set the property.
![../../_images/appearance-quick-set-color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/appearance-quick-set-color-brush.png)
Tip
To quickly edit a brush, in the Properties next to the Background Brush or Foreground Brush property click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) and edit the brush.
![../../_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png)


## Filling 2D nodes with a texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-texture "Link to this heading")
Use a Texture Brush to fill a 2D node with a texture.
To fill a 2D node with a texture:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures, select Texture Brush, and name the brush.
![../../_images/create-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-texture-brush.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select the 2D node that you want to fill with the brush you created, in the Properties add the Background Brush or the Foreground Brush property, and select the brush you created in the first step.
For example, create a Grid Layout 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to the brush you created in the first step.
![../../_images/grid-layout-2d-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-in-project.png) ![../../_images/grid-layout-2d-background-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-background-texture-brush.png)
  3. In the Properties click ![go-to-item](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/go-to-selected-item.png) next to the property that you added in the previous step to go to the brush used by that property, set the texture you want this texture brush to use, and adjust how the Texture Brush uses that texture:
     * Brush Modulate Color sets the modulation color for the brush.
     * Brush Horizontal Tiling affects the scale of the texture coordinates to set the horizontal tiling of the texture.
     * Brush Vertical Tiling affects the scale of the texture coordinates to set the vertical tiling of the texture.
     * Brush Texture sets the texture for the brush.
![../../_images/go-to-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/go-to-texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush-properties.png)


## Filling 2D nodes with a material[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-material "Link to this heading")
Use a Material Brush to fill a 2D node with a material.
To fill a 2D node with a material:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures, select Material Brush, and name the brush.
![../../_images/create-material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-material-brush.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Material property to the material you want to use to fill a 2D node.
If you do not have any materials in your project, create a material. See [Creating a material](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-materials.html#creating-a-material).
![../../_images/material-brush-set-material-to-colortexturematerial.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush-set-material-to-colortexturematerial.png) ![../../_images/colortexturematerial-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/colortexturematerial-properties.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the 2D node that you want to fill with the brush you created, in the Properties add the Background Brush or the Foreground Brush property, and select the brush you created in the first step.
For example, create a Button 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to the brush you created in the first step.
![../../_images/button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-properties-and-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-properties-and-preview.png)
  4. To adjust the appearance of the material, set the Material properties either in:
     * The Material Brush.
For example, to change the ambient color, texture, and blending of the material for the Material Brush, add and set the Ambient Color, Texture, and Blend Mode properties.
![../../_images/set-material-properties-in-material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-material-properties-in-material-brush.png)
     * The node which uses the Material Brush.
For example, to change the ambient color, texture, and blending of the material for a node, add and set the Ambient Color, Texture, and Blend Mode properties in that node.
![../../_images/set-material-properties-in-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-material-properties-in-node.png)


## Setting the color of text in 2D text nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#setting-the-color-of-text-in-2d-text-nodes "Link to this heading")
To set the color of text in a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node:
  1. In the Node Tree create or select a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node.
![../../_images/select-text-block-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-text-block-2d.png)
  2. In the Properties add the Foreground Brush property.
![../../_images/add-foreground-brush-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-foreground-brush-property.png)
  3. Set the Foreground Brush property to an existing Color Brush or select + Color Brush, name the brush, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) next to the property, and set the color of the Color Brush you created.
![../../_images/select-and-set-color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-and-set-color-brush.png)
Tip
To quickly edit a brush, in the Properties next to the Background Brush or Foreground Brush property click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) and edit the brush.
![../../_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png)


## Controlling the appearance of brushes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#controlling-the-appearance-of-brushes "Link to this heading")
You can define the appearance of brushes in different application states. For example, when you use a brush to fill a Button 2D node, you can change the appearance of the brush when the user presses the button.
To control the appearance of a brush, create a state manager which sets the properties of the brush in the node which uses the brush.
To control the appearance of a brush:
  1. Create a brush and use it to fill a 2D node.
For example, create a texture brush and set the Background Brush property of a Button 2D node to the texture brush that you created. See [Filling 2D nodes with a texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-texture).
![../../_images/my-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-with-background-my-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-with-background-my-texture-brush.png)
  2. Create a state manager which you use to control the appearance of the brush that you created in the first step.
For example:
    1. Create for the Button 2D node a state manager that has two states named Released and Pressed and set the state manager to use the Button > Is Down controller property. See [Using a state manager to set button states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html#using-a-state-manager-to-set-button-states).
![../../_images/button-2d-state-manager-for-setting-texture-brush-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-state-manager-for-setting-texture-brush-properties.png)
    2. Set the appearance of the brush in the Released and Pressed states.
For example, in the Properties next to the Background Brush property click ![quick-edit-properties](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png), set the Brush Modulate Color property, and in the State Tools click ![store-current-values](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/store-current-values.png) in the Pressed state to save the property value to the Pressed state.
![../../_images/my-texture-brush-set-properties-for-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-texture-brush-set-properties-for-state.png) ![../../_images/set-brush-properties-to-pressed-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-brush-properties-to-pressed-state.png)


Now when you interact with the node in the Preview, Kanzi changes the appearance of the brush that you created.
## Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#applying-custom-rendering-to-2d-nodes "Link to this heading")
Apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects.
For example, you can convert color images in a 2D node to grayscale.
To apply custom rendering to a 2D node, use the Composition Brush property to compose the node on the screen with a Material Brush, and enable the Force Composition property.
To apply custom rendering to a 2D node:
  1. Create a material with which you want to apply custom rendering.
For example, to create a material that converts color to grayscale:
    1. In the Library, press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures and select Material Type. Kanzi Studio creates a material type and a material that uses the material type.
![../../_images/create-material-type.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-material-type.png) ![../../_images/material-type-and-its-material-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-type-and-its-material-in-library.png)
    2. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Material Types, expand the material type that you created. Double-click the Vertex Shader to open it in the Shader Source Editor, replace the existing shader code with this code, and save the shader.

```
#version 310 es

in vec3 kzPosition;
in vec2 kzTextureCoordinate0;
uniform highp mat4 kzProjectionCameraWorldMatrix;

out mediump vec2 vTexCoord;

void main()
{
    precision mediump float;
    vTexCoord = kzTextureCoordinate0;
    gl_Position = kzProjectionCameraWorldMatrix * vec4(kzPosition.xyz, 1.0);
}

```
Copy to clipboard
    3. Open the Fragment Shader, replace the existing shader code with the code in this step, and save the shader.
In the shader, use these Kanzi default uniforms:
       * `ContentTexture` to define the texture that the rendered node provides when rendering
       * `RenderOpacity` to define the opacity of the rendered node
See [Shader uniforms](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/editing-shaders.html#shader-uniforms).

```
#version 310 es

uniform sampler2D ContentTexture;
in mediump vec2 vTexCoord;
uniform lowp float RenderOpacity;
layout(location = 0) out vec4 fragColor;

void main()
{
    precision mediump float;
    // Use this algorithm to convert the colors in the texture used by
    // the 2D node to grayscale.
    // To integrate to the Kanzi rendering pipeline, the shader must output
    // premultiplied alpha.
    vec4 color = texture(ContentTexture, vTexCoord);
    float grayscale = dot(color.rgb, vec3(0.21, 0.72, 0.07));
    float alpha = color.a * RenderOpacity;
    vec3 premultipliedColor = vec3(grayscale) * alpha;
    fragColor = vec4(premultipliedColor, alpha);
}

```
Copy to clipboard
  2. In the Library, press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures and select Material Brush. In the Properties, set the Material property to the material that you created in the previous step.
![../../_images/create-material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-material-brush.png) ![../../_images/set-material-to-material-type-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-material-to-material-type-material.png)
  3. In the Node Tree, create or select a 2D node to which you want to apply the material that you created. For example, create a Stack Layout 2D node. In the Stack Layout 2D node, create an Image node.
![../../_images/stack-layout-with-image-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-with-image-node.png)
  4. In the Properties, add and set:
     * Brush Composition Brush to the material brush that uses the material you want to apply to that node
     * Node 2D > Force Composition to enabled
     * (Optional) Render Target > Multisample Level to the number of anti-aliasing samples that you want to apply to the content
     * (Optional) Node > Opacity to control the translucency of the node
![../../_images/stack-layout-with-applied-composition-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-with-applied-composition-brush.png)


## Using brushes in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#using-brushes-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `Brush[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a12410.html)` class.
##  Brush property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#brush-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for brushes, see [Brush](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/brush-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#sa "Link to this heading")

sub_documents.title: Buttons
sub_documents.summary: This page introduces the button types available in Kanzi: Button 3D/2D for click/tap interactions, Toggle Button 3D/2D for multiple toggle states, and Toggle Button Group 3D/2D for mutually exclusive selection. It provides links to detailed usage guides and tutorials for each button type.

Use buttons to create interactions through clicking the objects contained within buttons.
Kanzi has these buttons:

![../../_images/toggle-button1.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button1.gif)
