sub_documents.title: Camera node
sub_documents.summary: This page describes the Camera node in Kanzi Studio, which is used to display the content of a Scene in the Preview and in the final application. It explains that multiple Camera nodes can be set up in different ways but only one can be active at a time to view a scene. The Camera property in each Scene determines which camera is used for the final view. In the Preview, a grey movie camera pictograph represents the camera node, and the lens of the camera defines the point of view. The page also mentions that when creating a new project, a Camera node is automatically included in the Viewport 2D > Scene node. It provides tips for viewing Camera nodes in the Preview (using Analyze mode and Debug objects) and links to related topics on using the Camera node and making objects turn to a camera.

# Camera node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/cameras.html#camera-node "Link to this heading")

Use the Camera node to show the content of a Scene in Kanzi Studio Preview and in your Kanzi application.
To change the view of a Scene, you can use several Camera nodes and set them in different ways, but you can use only one Camera node at a time to view a scene. In each Scene, use the Camera property to set the camera that you want to use for the final view of your Kanzi application.
In the Preview, a grey movie camera pictograph represents the camera node. The lens of the camera is the point of view from which the content of a Scene is shown.
Tip
To see Camera nodes in the Preview, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode, right-click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Debug objects.
![../../_images/camera1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera1.png)
When you create a Kanzi Studio project, the Viewport 2D > Scene node contains a Camera node that shows that Scene in the Preview. See [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).

sub_documents.title: Color workflow
sub_documents.summary: This Kanzi documentation page explains the color workflow options in Kanzi, covering linear and nonlinear gamma color spaces. It details the standard (nonlinear gamma) color workflow, which is the default, and the linear color workflow, which provides more accurate lighting and blending. The page includes instructions for configuring images, color property bindings, shaders, and graphics API requirements for the linear workflow, as well as steps for converting applications from standard to linear color workflow.

## Linear and nonlinear gamma color spaces[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#linear-and-nonlinear-gamma-color-spaces "Link to this heading")
The purpose of the sRGB color space is to represent colors for display on computer monitors. Currently sRGB is the standard for the nonlinear gamma color space. It is needed because human perception of light is nonlinear, and computer monitors have a nonlinear response to light intensity.
The human eye distinguishes between darker shades better than lighter shades. For this reason it makes sense to preserve more accuracy for dark intensities when storing and displaying images on screens. The nonlinear gamma color space achieves this with gamma correction, which puts the intensity of each pixel in an image through a power function:
Iγ
Images are usually stored with an encoding gamma applied to them, and screens apply a decoding gamma. This image shows the graphs of the gamma transfer functions that Kanzi uses to convert between the linear and gamma color spaces.
![../../_images/gamma.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/gamma.svg)
This image shows a gradient where the intensity of the light emitted by your screen increases linearly.
![../../_images/linear_emitted_intensity.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear_emitted_intensity.png)
Applying a decoding gamma to the above gradient results in this gradient where the perceptual light intensity increases linearly.
![../../_images/linear_perceptual_intensity.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear_perceptual_intensity.png)
The problem with the nonlinear gamma color space is its unsuitability for graphics operations. Performing color calculations in nonlinear space leads to inaccurate results in color and alpha blending. Linear color space is needed for mathematically correct lighting and color blending calculations.
In linear color space numerical intensity values correspond to their actual intensity, which makes it possible to add and multiply color values correctly. Linear color space rendering provides more accurate results and more realistic surface shading, particularly with physically based rendering techniques.
These images show an example of blending in nonlinear gamma (left) and linear (right) color space. Blending in nonlinear gamma color space results in overly bright blends and saturated bands.
[![../../_images/legacy-blending.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/legacy-blending.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/legacy-blending.png) [![../../_images/linear-blending.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear-blending.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear-blending.png)
Kanzi by default uses the the nonlinear gamma, or standard, color workflow, where Kanzi operates on color values in the gamma color space. See [Using the standard color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-standard-color-workflow).
Kanzi also supports the linear color workflow, where Kanzi operates on color values in linear color space. See [Using the linear color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-linear-color-workflow) and [Converting applications from standard to linear color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#converting-applications-from-standard-to-linear-color-workflow).
## Using the linear color workflow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-linear-color-workflow "Link to this heading")
In the linear color workflow Kanzi enables realistic lighting computations and correct color blending. To achieve accurate rendering of color and light, Kanzi converts all color values to linear color space before performing operations on them. Kanzi then converts the color values back to the gamma color space for storage or display.
### Images[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#images "Link to this heading")
To configure the images in your Kanzi Studio project for linear color workflow:
  * In the Library > Resource Files > Images for each image resource that uses the ASTC, ETC2, JPEG, or PNG format set the value of the sRGB Content property:
    * If the image contains sRGB color information, set the sRGB Content property to enabled. This is the default setting.
If you disable the sRGB Content property for an image that contains sRGB color information, Kanzi can render the textures that use the image brighter than expected.
    * If the image contains non-color information, such as a normal, roughness, or occlusion map, set the sRGB Content property to disabled.
Textures that contain non-color information are stored in linear format. By disabling the sRGB Content property you set Kanzi to pass the image data to a shader directly, without performing a color space conversion.
![../../_images/srgb-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/srgb-content.png)
  * Kanzi by default premultiplies the alpha channel of images in linear color space. To premultiply the alpha channel in the color space of the image, in the Library > Resource Files > Images select an image and in the Properties disable the Linear Premultiply property. See [Preparing images in third-party tools](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/preparing-images-in-3rd-party-tools.html).
![../../_images/linear-premultiply.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear-premultiply.png)


### Color property bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#color-property-bindings "Link to this heading")
To set color values in binding expressions in the linear color workflow:
  * Specify `Color4` values in sRGB color space. See [color4](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#id1).
For example:

```
Color4(0, 0.75, 0.25, 1)

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/r0g192b64.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/r0g192b64.png)
  * Specify the values of individual RGB color channels in linear color space.
Use the [sRGBToLinear](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#srgbtolinear) binding function to convert a color channel value to linear color space.
For example:
    * This binding expression is equal to `Color4(0, 0.75, 0.25, 1)`:

```
color = Color4(0, 0, 0, 1)
color.g = sRGBToLinear(0.75)
color.b = sRGBToLinear(0.25)
color

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/r0g192b64.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/r0g192b64.png)
    * This binding expression is equal to `Color4(0, 0.879, 0.535, 1)`:

```
color = Color4(0, 0, 0, 1)
color.g = 0.75
color.b = 0.25
color

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/r0g225b137.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/r0g225b137.png)


### Shaders[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#shaders "Link to this heading")
In the linear color workflow shaders expect color input to be in linear color space and they output color in linear color space. To preserve accuracy when storing color values in 8-bit per channel texture formats, Kanzi converts the color values back to the sRGB color space before storing.
### Graphics API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#graphics-api "Link to this heading")
The linear color workflow needs either:
  * EGL version 1.5 or later, or EGL version 1.4 with the `EGL_KHR_gl_colorspace` extension.
  * Vulkan 1.1 or later.


## Using the standard color workflow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-standard-color-workflow "Link to this heading")
By default Kanzi uses the standard color workflow. This performs operations on color values in the nonlinear gamma color space. This provides less precise rendering results than the linear color workflow.
Use the standard color workflow when you:
  * Deploy your application to a device that does not support linear color space.
To support linear color space, your target platform must implement EGL version 1.5 or later, or EGL version 1.4 with the `EGL_KHR_gl_colorspace` extension, or Vulkan 1.1 or later.
When your Kanzi application requests linear color space but the target device does not support it, the resulting behavior varies between target platforms.
For example, your application can:
    * Print to the log a warning about lack of support for EGL_GL_COLORSPACE, and fall back to the legacy color space.
    * Terminate with this error:

```
eglCreateWindowSurface() failed: EGL_BAD_ATTRIBUTE

```
Copy to clipboard
  * Migrate a project from earlier versions of Kanzi.


In the standard color workflow Kanzi does not convert color input. If you use the Kanzi Engine API to create a `ColorRGBA[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a14966.html)` object, provide the color values in the sRGB color space.
To use the standard color workflow:
  1. Configure your application to use an unspecified color space by setting either:
     * In `application.cfg`:

```
SurfaceColorSpace = "standard"

```
Copy to clipboard
     * In the C++ application in the `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` function:

```
configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.colorSpace = "standard";

```
Copy to clipboard
See [SurfaceColorSpace](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#surfacecolorspace).
  2. In Kanzi Studio in the Project > Properties set the Color Workflow property to Standard.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/color-workflow-legacy.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-workflow-legacy.png)
  3. Write your shaders to output colors in the gamma space of your target display, which is likely sRGB. See [Shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/shaders.html).


## Converting applications from standard to linear color workflow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#converting-applications-from-standard-to-linear-color-workflow "Link to this heading")
To convert your application from the standard color workflow to the linear color workflow:
  1. Configure your application to use the sRGB color space by configuring the linear color workflow:
     * In `application.cfg`:

```
SurfaceColorSpace = "srgb"

```
Copy to clipboard
     * In the C++ application in the `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` function:

```
configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.colorSpace = "srgb";

```
Copy to clipboard
See [SurfaceColorSpace](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#surfacecolorspace).
  2. In Kanzi Studio in the Project > Properties set Color Workflow to Linear.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/color-workflow-linear.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-workflow-linear.png)
  3. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Material Types for each material type make sure that:
     * Bindings do not contain needless manually added sRGB conversions.
For example, you do not need to use the [linearTosRGB](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#lineartosrgb) binding function to convert color values from linear color space to sRGB color space. In the linear color workflow shaders expect color input to be in linear color space.
     * Shaders do not apply gamma correction at input or output.
In the linear color workflow shaders expect color input to be in linear color space and they output color in linear color space.
  4. In the Library > Resource Files > Images for each image resource that uses the ASTC, ETC2, JPEG, or PNG format check that the sRGB Content property is set correctly:
     * If the image contains sRGB color information, set the sRGB Content property to enabled. This is the default setting.
If you disable the sRGB Content property for an image that contains sRGB color information, Kanzi can render the textures that use the image brighter than expected.
     * If the image contains non-color information, such as a normal, roughness, or occlusion map, set the sRGB Content property to disabled.
Textures that contain non-color information are stored in linear format. By disabling the sRGB Content property you set Kanzi to pass the image data to a shader directly, without performing a color space conversion.
![../../_images/srgb-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/srgb-content.png)
  5. To get the desired color blending result, adjust the partially transparent colors in your project where needed.
For example, nodes filled with these color brushes look different in the standard and linear color workflow modes:
![../../_images/red-green-blue-brushes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/red-green-blue-brushes.png)  
| Standard color workflow  | Linear color workflow  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ![../../_images/color-brush-blending-legacy.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush-blending-legacy.png)  |  ![../../_images/color-brush-blending-linear.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush-blending-linear.png)  |  


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#sa "Link to this heading")

sub_documents.title: Using the Content Layout nodes
sub_documents.summary: This page explains how to use Content Layout nodes in Kanzi to present content as a single item, such as a button with border, background, icon, and label. It covers creating Content Layout 2D/3D nodes, setting padding and margins, adapting to content size or fixed size, aligning content, and setting appearance. It also mentions API classes and related layout nodes.

# Using the Content Layout nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#using-the-content-layout-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Content Layout nodes to present content in a UI control as a single item.
For example, use a Content Layout node to create the layout for a list item or a button with a border, a background, an icon, and a label.
![../../_images/content-layout.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout.gif)
By default the size of a Content Layout node is determined by the size of its child nodes. A Content Layout node that does not have child nodes by default stretches to take all the available space.
A Content Layout node does not arrange its child nodes. To arrange nodes in a Content Layout node, use another layout control node. See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html).
Content Layout allows you to create layouts where:
  * Content of a Content Layout node determines the size of the Content Layout node. See [Creating a Content Layout node that adapts to the size of its content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-content-layout-adapts-to-size).
  * Content of a Content Layout node adapts to the size that you set. See [Creating a Content Layout where content adapts to a fixed size](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-content-layout-fixed-size).


## Creating a Content Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-a-content-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Content Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Content Layout node and select either Content Layout 3D, or Content Layout 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/create-content-layout-2d-in-root-page.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-content-layout-2d-in-root-page.png)
  2. In the Node Tree add content to the Content Layout node.
For example, if you created a Content Layout 2D node, create a Text Block 2D node.
Content Layout node does not arrange its child nodes. To arrange nodes in a Content Layout node, use another layout control node. See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html).
  3. To add space around the content of the Content Layout node, in the Node Tree select the Content Layout node, and in the Properties add and set the padding properties:
     * Depth Padding to add space in the back and front of the content in a Content Layout 3D node
     * Horizontal Padding to add space on the left and the right sides of the content
     * Vertical Padding to add space on the bottom and the top of the content
![../../_images/content-layout-2d-padding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-padding.png)


## Creating a Content Layout node that adapts to the size of its content[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-a-content-layout-node-that-adapts-to-the-size-of-its-content "Link to this heading")
You can use a Content Layout node to create a layout that adapts to the size of its content. In this example, you create the layout of a 2D button with a border, a background, an icon, and a label.
To create a Content Layout node that adapts to the size of its content:
  1. In the Node Tree create a Button 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to a brush that you want to use to fill the Button 2D node. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
You fill the Button 2D node with a brush to show the border of the button.
For example, select + Color Brush, name the brush, click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) next to the Background Brush property, and set the color of the color brush.
![../../_images/button-2d-in-root-page.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-in-root-page.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-background-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-background-brush.png)
  2. In the Button 2D node create a Content Layout 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to a brush that you want to use to fill the Content Layout 2D node.
The Content Layout 2D node stretches the button to take all the available space.
![../../_images/create-content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png) ![../../_images/content-layout-2d-background-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-background-brush.png)
  3. Add content to the Content Layout node.
For example, create a Stack Layout 2D node, and in the Stack Layout 2D node create:
     * Image node and in the Properties add and set:
       * Image to a texture that shows the button icon
       * Vertical Alignment to Center
       * Horizontal Margin property Right property field to add space on the right side of the Image node
     * Text Block 2D node and in the Properties add and set:
       * Text to set the button label
       * Vertical Alignment to Center
The Content Layout 2D node takes the space needed by the content that you add to it.
![../../_images/stack-layout-in-content-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-in-content-layout.png) ![../../_images/image-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-properties1.png) ![../../_images/text-block-2d-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-properties1.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview-initial.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview-initial.png)
  4. In the Node Tree select the Content Layout 2D node and in the Properties add and set:
     * Horizontal Padding and Vertical Padding to set the amount of space between the Content Layout 2D node and its parent node.
This way you set the amount of space between the button borders and content.
     * Horizontal Margin and Vertical Margin to set the thickness of the button border.
![../../_images/content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png) ![../../_images/content-layout-padding-and-margin.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-padding-and-margin.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview.png)


## Creating a Content Layout where content adapts to a fixed size[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-a-content-layout-where-content-adapts-to-a-fixed-size "Link to this heading")
You can use a Content Layout node to create a layout where the content adapts to the size that you set. In this example, you create the layout of a fixed-sized 2D button with a border, a background, an icon, and a label.
To create a Content Layout where content adapts to a fixed size:
  1. Create a 2D layout that adapts to the size of its content. See [Creating a Content Layout node that adapts to the size of its content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-content-layout-adapts-to-size).
  2. Set the size of the node that contains a Content Layout 2D node.
For example, in the Node Tree select the Button 2D node, and in the Properties add and set the Layout Width and Layout Height properties.
![../../_images/button-2d-with-content-in-root-page.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-with-content-in-root-page.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-size-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-size-set.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview-3.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview-3.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the Content Layout 2D node and in the Properties add and set:
     * Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment to Stretch
This way you set the Content Layout 2D node to take as much space on the x and y axis as it can.
     * Clip Children to enabled
This way you clip the content of the child nodes of the Content Layout 2D node to fit into the size of the Content Layout 2D node.
![../../_images/content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png) ![../../_images/content-layout-2d-alignment-stretch.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-alignment-stretch.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview-4.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview-4.png)
  4. Align the content of the Content Layout node.
For example, in the Node Tree select the Stack Layout 2D node, in the Properties add the Vertical Alignment property, and set it to Center.
![../../_images/stack-layout-in-content-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-in-content-layout.png) ![../../_images/stack-layout-alignment-center.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-alignment-center.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview-5.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview-5.png)


## Setting the appearance of a Content Layout 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#setting-the-appearance-of-a-content-layout-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)


## Using the Content Layout 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#using-the-content-layout-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")

sub_documents.title: Data sources
sub_documents.summary: This page introduces Kanzi data sources, explaining how they separate UI from application data and remove dependencies between Kanzi Studio projects and application code. It describes binding node/resource properties to data source values, typical use cases (speed, RPM, fuel, contacts, media, navigation), and points to tutorials and related documentation for defining and using data sources.

# Data sources[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/data-sources.html#data-sources "Link to this heading")

Use data sources to separate the user interface from the application data and to remove the dependencies between a Kanzi Studio project and the application code which define the Kanzi application.
Kanzi allows you to define the format and structure of your data source by defining a Kanzi Engine data source plugin.
When you use a data source in a Kanzi application you bind the values of properties and property fields to data that comes from a data source. This binding establishes a connection between a node or a resource and the application data. When data in the data source changes, the nodes and resources which are bound to the data reflect the change in the data.
A typical use case is to bind the properties of nodes in your cluster or IVI system to data from a data source provided by a server to which your application connects. For example, your Kanzi application can use data sources to get data such as speed, RPM, and fuel information, address book entries, album and song information, navigation information, and so on.
Learn how to define and use data sources in your Kanzi applications by completing the data sources tutorial. See [Tutorial: Get application data from a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-sources/data-sources.html).

sub_documents.title: Deploying Kanzi applications
sub_documents.summary: This page explains how to deploy Kanzi applications to various target platforms. It covers supported platforms (Windows, Linux, Android, iOS, QNX, Integrity, Nucleus), build tools (Visual Studio 2022 on Windows, CMake for non-Windows), and the platform configuration packages created by Kanzi Studio. It also lists the graphics backends (OpenGL ES, Vulkan) and CPU architectures supported for each platform, and notes that additional platform support can be requested from Rightware sales.

While you develop Kanzi applications using Kanzi Studio and Visual Studio on Windows, you can compile your Kanzi applications for and execute on any mobile or embedded platform that supports OpenGL ES 3.0 or Vulkan 1.1.
Kanzi platform packages come with build configuration files and scripts that you can modify to adjust them to your build environment.
## Supported platforms[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications.html#supported-platforms "Link to this heading")
To deploy your Kanzi application to a target platform, you have to build it for the target platform. The output of building activity is an executable or an installer package that you can run or install on a target device. Kanzi supports building using Visual Studio 2022 on Windows and CMake for non-Windows platforms.
When you create your Kanzi application with a C++ application in Kanzi Studio, Kanzi creates a set of platform configurations. Kanzi creates platform configurations in `<ProjectName>/Application/configs/platforms`.
These platform packages are available with a Kanzi installation:
  * Android (ARM, Aarch64, x86, x86_64). See [Deploying Kanzi applications to Android](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications-for-android.html).

sub_documents.title: Using the Dock Layout nodes
sub_documents.summary: This page from the Kanzi documentation explains how to use Dock Layout nodes (Dock Layout 2D and Dock Layout 3D) to arrange child nodes relative to each other along the sides of the layout. It describes the subtractive layout mechanism, the Side property (Left, Right, Top, Bottom), the Last Item Fill property, margin properties (Depth, Horizontal, Vertical), and how to create a Dock Layout node in the Node Tree. It also covers setting the appearance of 2D nodes, API references for DockLayout2D and DockLayout3D classes, and links to related layout documentation.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Using the Dock Layout nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-dock-layouts.html#using-the-dock-layout-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Dock Layout nodes to place nodes relative to each other along the sides of a Dock Layout node.
A Dock Layout node arranges its items in a subtractive way: after positioning the first node, the Dock Layout node uses the remaining space to position the next node, and so on. When arranging its child nodes, a Dock Layout node uses its entire size.
You set the side along which you want to place a node in a Dock Layout node with the Side property.
![../../_images/dock-layout.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dock-layout.gif)
A Dock Layout node arranges its items in a subtractive way: after positioning the first node, the Dock Layout node uses the remaining space to position the next node, and so on. When arranging its child nodes, a Dock Layout node uses its entire size.
Dock Layout nodes determine the position of their child nodes by:
  * The order in which the child nodes appear in the node tree.
  * The value of the Side property in each child node of a Dock Layout node. The Dock Layout node sets each child node to occupy that entire side.
  * The number of the child nodes in a Dock Layout node.

![../../_images/dock-layout-how-it-works.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dock-layout-how-it-works.gif)
## Creating a Dock Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-dock-layouts.html#creating-a-dock-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Dock Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Dock Layout node and select either Dock Layout 3D, or Dock Layout 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/node-tree-create-dock-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-create-dock-layout-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Dock Layout 3D, add several Plane nodes, if you created a Dock Layout 2D, add several Image nodes.
As you add child nodes, the Dock Layout node automatically positions them.
![../../_images/node-tree-dock-layout-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-dock-layout-images.png) ![../../_images/preview-dock-layout-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-dock-layout-images.png)
  3. In the Node Tree, select all child nodes of the Dock Layout node. In the Properties, add the Dock Layout > Side property and set it to:
     * Left to set the child node to occupy the left part of the Dock Layout node.
     * Right to set the child node to occupy the right part of the Dock Layout node.
     * Top to set the child node to occupy the top part of the Dock Layout node.
     * Bottom to set the child node to occupy the bottom part of the Dock Layout node.
For example, set the Side property for:
     * Image to Top
     * Button to Bottom
     * Temperature-F to Right
     * Condition to Right
     * Temperature-C to Left
![../../_images/dock-layout-add-side-property-to-child-node.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dock-layout-add-side-property-to-child-node.gif)
  4. (Optional) When you want the last child node in a Dock Layout node to occupy the remaining space of the Dock Layout node, add to the Dock Layout node the Last Item Fill property, and enable it.
  5. (Optional) To clear the area around child nodes in a layout, in the Node Tree select child nodes in the layout, in the Properties click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png), and add and set the margin properties:
     * Depth Margin to clear the area in the back and the front of a child node.
     * Horizontal Margin to clear the area on the left and the right sides of a child node.
     * Vertical Margin to clear the area on the bottom and the top of a child node.
![../../_images/dock-layout-add-margin.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dock-layout-add-margin.gif)


## Setting the appearance of a Dock Layout 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-dock-layouts.html#setting-the-appearance-of-a-dock-layout-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).

sub_documents.title: Using the Empty Node nodes
sub_documents.summary: This page describes the Empty Node nodes in Kanzi, which are used to group nodes and set property values for child nodes. Empty Nodes have no visual representation by default and no specific properties. They allow absolute positioning, do not restrict child movement, and are not compacting layouts. The page covers creating Empty Node 2D and 3D nodes, setting appearance for 2D nodes, using them in the API, and provides links to property types and messages.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Using the Empty Node nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#using-the-empty-node-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Empty Node nodes to group nodes and to set property values of their child nodes.
By default, Empty Node nodes do not have a visual representation, or any functionality other than a transparent background and that they can act as a parent node to other nodes. Empty Node nodes do not have any properties specific only to them.
For example, use Empty Node nodes to:
  * Edit the origin of nodes. See [Editing the origin of nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/editing-the-origin-of-nodes.html).
  * Apply transformation to all its child nodes. See [Tutorial: Create reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/reflections/reflections.html).
  * Replace the root node of a node prefab. See [Replacing the root node of a node prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#replacing-the-root-node-of-a-node-prefab).


An Empty Node is a node into which you can put any other node and has these properties:
  * It allows absolute positioning of its child nodes.
  * Does not restrict the movement of its child nodes.
  * Is not a compacting layout.


Empty Node does not have inherent layout characteristics. Empty Node does not resize its child nodes, but places them to a position you specify. The default values of the Layout Height and Layout Width properties of an Empty Node are 0, but it stretches by default to take all the space its child nodes need.
You can use the Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment properties to align the child nodes of an Empty Node only after you specify the Layout Height and Layout Width properties of that Empty Node.
## Creating an Empty Node node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#creating-an-empty-node-node "Link to this heading")
To create an Empty Node node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create an Empty Node node and select either Empty Node 3D, or Empty Node 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
  2. In the Node Tree add items to the Empty Node node.
For example, if you created an Empty Node 3D node, add Sphere nodes, if you created an Empty Node 2D node, add Image nodes.
  3. (Optional) In the Node Tree select the Empty Node node, in the Properties click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png), add and set the property you want all its child nodes to inherit.


## Setting the appearance of an Empty Node 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-an-empty-node-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)


## Using the Empty Node 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#using-the-empty-node-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create an Empty Node 3D node using the API:

```
// Create an Empty Node 3D named Empty3D
EmptyNode3DSharedPtr emptyNode = EmptyNode3D::create(domain, "Empty3D");

// Create and add a cube to the Empty Node 3D
ModelSharedPtr cube = Model::createCube(domain, "Cube", 1.0f, KanziThemeOrange);
emptyNode->addChild(cube);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `EmptyNode3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13750.html)` class.
## Using the Empty Node 2D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#using-the-empty-node-2d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create an Empty Node 2D node using the API:

```
// Create an Empty Node 2D named Empty2D
EmptyNode2DSharedPtr empty2D = EmptyNode2D::create(domain, "Empty2D");

// Create and add an Image to the Empty Node 2D
ImageSharedPtr image = Image::create(domain, "Image");
image->setTextureResourceID(ResourceID("DefaultTexture"));
empty2D->addChild(image);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `EmptyNode2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13746.html)` class.
##  Empty Node property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#empty-node-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For lists of the available property types and messages for the Empty Node nodes, see [Empty Node 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/empty-node-2d-reference.html) and [Empty Node 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/empty-node-3d-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Property system](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/property-system.html)
[Property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/property-types.html)
[Tutorial: Create reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/reflections/reflections.html)
[Editing the origin of nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/editing-the-origin-of-nodes.html)

sub_documents.title: Factory Content assets
sub_documents.summary: This page describes the Factory Content assets in Kanzi Studio, which are ready-made components and materials for faster prototyping. It covers 2D interactivity controls (Button, Checkbox, Radio Buttons, Slider, Toggle Button), progress components (Processing Indicator, Progress Bar, Progress Indicator), list components (Contact List, Cover Flow, Poster Flow), complete UI components (Car, Music Player, Navigation Bar, Notification Popup, Traditional Gauges), and materials (Aluminium, Car Paint, Carbon Fiber, Chrome, Glass, Leather, Mask Texture, Rubber). It explains how to use these assets by dragging them from the Asset Packages to the Node Tree, Prefabs, or Preview, and mentions properties for customization.

#  Factory Content assets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#factory-content-assets "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

The Factory Content asset packages contain ready-made components and materials that you can use to create prototype projects faster.
Here you can find all the Factory Content assets:
  * 2D interactivity control components that you can use to make your application interactive. See [Interactivity control components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#interactivity-control-components).
  * Progress components that you can use to indicate that a task is in progress. See [Progress components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-components).
  * List components that you can use to present collections of items arranged in scrollable lists. See [List components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#list-components).
  * Complete user interface components that you can use to add functionality to your application. See [Complete user interface components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#complete-user-interface-components).
  * Materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project. See [Materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#materials).
  * Render Passes that you can use to add effects to your project. See [Render Passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#render-passes).


To use the Factory Content assets in your Kanzi Studio project, from the Asset Packages drag an asset to a node in the Node Tree, to the Prefabs, or to the Preview. See [Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html).
![../../_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png)
## Interactivity control components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#interactivity-control-components "Link to this heading")
Use 2D interactivity control components to make your application interactive.
###  Button[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#button "Link to this heading")
Use the Button to create a button that receives user input.
![../../_images/button.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button.gif)
To adjust the appearance and behavior of the Button, after you add the Button to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Label to set the text in the button.
  * Main Color to set the color of the button background.
  * Highlight Color to set the color of the button background when the user presses the button.
  * Border Color to set the color of the button border that is visible when the user presses the button.
  * Border Thickness to set the width of the button border that is visible when the user presses the button.
  * Rounding Radius to set the roundness of the button corners.
For example, to make the button corners right-angle, set Rounding Radius to 0.

![../../_images/button-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-properties.png)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the button reacts to user input. See [Using the Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
The Button uses a state manager that sets the appearance and behavior of the Button when:
  * The user presses the button.
  * The value of the Enabled property changes.
When you disable the Enabled property in the Button node, the button does not react to user input.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.png)


###  Checkbox[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#checkbox "Link to this heading")
Use the Checkbox to create a checkbox that receives user input.
![../../_images/checkbox.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/checkbox.gif)
The Checkbox uses a state manager that sets the appearance and behavior of the Checkbox when:
  * The user toggles the checkbox.
  * The value of the Enabled property changes.
When you disable the Enabled property in the Checkbox node, the checkbox does not react to user input.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.png)


###  Radio Buttons[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#radio-buttons "Link to this heading")
Use the Radio Buttons to create radio buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/radio-buttons.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/radio-buttons.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how radio buttons react to user input. See [Using the Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
###  Slider[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#slider "Link to this heading")
Use the Slider to create a slider that receives user input.
![../../_images/slider1.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider1.gif)
To adjust the appearance and behavior of the Slider, after you add the Slider to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Maximum Value to set the highest value of the slider. The default value is 100.
  * Minimum Value to set the lowest value of the slider. The default value is 0.
  * Step Value to set the increment by which the knob moves on the rail. The default value is 1.
  * Value to set the initial position of the knob on the rail. You can use bindings to control another property with the position of the slider. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
  * Knob Style to set the shape of the knob to square or circle, or to not show the knob.
  * Knob Size to set the size of the knob.
  * Knob Color to set the color of the knob.
  * Rail Thickness to set the thickness of the rail.
  * Rail Rounded Ends to set whether to round the ends of the rail.
  * Rail Background Color to set the color of the rail from the knob until the end of the rail.
  * Rail Fill Color to set the color of the rail from the start of the rail until the knob.

![../../_images/slider-range-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-range-properties1.png) ![../../_images/slider-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-properties.png)
The Slider uses a state manager that sets the appearance and behavior of the slider when the value of the Enabled property changes. When you disable the Enabled property in the Slider node, the slider does not react to user input.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.png)
###  Toggle Button[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#toggle-button "Link to this heading")
Use the Toggle Button to create a toggle button that receives user input.
![../../_images/toggle-button.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button.gif)
The Toggle Button uses a state manager that sets the appearance of the Toggle Button when the user toggles it.
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the toggle button reacts to user input. See [Using the Toggle Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
## Progress components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-components "Link to this heading")
Use the progress components to show that a task is in progress.
###  Processing Indicator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#processing-indicator "Link to this heading")
Use the Processing Indicator to show that the application is processing a task.
![../../_images/processing-indicator.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator.gif)
To adjust the appearance of the Processing Indicator, after you add the Processing Indicator to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Color to set the color of the processing indicator.
  * Masked to set whether to mask the processing indicator with the texture that you set using the Masking Texture property.
  * Masking Texture to a texture to use to mask the processing indicator.
In the masking texture:
    * Black pixels form the mask that hides areas of the processing indicator.
    * White pixels form the gaps in the mask that show areas of the processing indicator.
By default the Processing Indicator is masked by a texture that shows a ring of circles.
  * Offset to set the rotation angle of the processing indicator.
  * Step Count to set the number of segments in the processing indicator.

![../../_images/processing-indicator-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator-properties.png)
###  Progress Bar[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-bar "Link to this heading")
Use the Progress Bar to show that a task is in progress, expressed both visually and as a percentage.
![../../_images/progress-bar.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-bar.gif)
To set the value of the Progress Bar, in the Properties set the value of the Progress property. You can use bindings to control the Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
To set the length of the gradient in the end of the progress bar, in the Properties set the value of the Smoothing property.
![../../_images/progress-bar-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-bar-properties.png)
###  Progress Indicator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-indicator "Link to this heading")
Use the Progress Indicator to show that a task is in progress, expressed both visually and as a percentage.
![../../_images/progress-indicator.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-indicator.gif)
To set the value of the Progress Indicator, in the Properties set the value of the Progress property. You can use bindings to control the Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
To adjust the appearance of the Progress Indicator, after you add the Progress Indicator to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Brush Color to set the color of the progress indicator ring.
  * Progress Smoothness to set the length of the gradient in the end of the progress indicator.
  * Ring Smoothness to set the edge smoothness of the progress indicator ring.
  * Ring Thickness to set the width of the progress indicator ring.

![../../_images/progress-indicator-brush-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-indicator-brush-color.png) ![../../_images/progress-indicator-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-indicator-properties1.png)
## List components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#list-components "Link to this heading")
Use the list components to present collections of items arranged in scrollable lists.
Each list component uses a List Box node to arrange its items. See [List Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html).
Use a data source to display your own data in a list component. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html), and [Tutorial: Get application data from a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-sources/data-sources.html).
###  Contact List[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#contact-list "Link to this heading")
Use the Contact List to create a contact list that shows the name, profile picture, and phone number for each contact.
![../../_images/contact-list.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contact-list.gif)
To set the content and behavior of the Contact List, in the Properties add and set:
  * Items Source to provide a data source for the list items.
  * Selection Behavior to set whether the list box brings an item to the center of the list box area when the user selects that item.

###  Cover Flow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#cover-flow "Link to this heading")
Use the Cover Flow to present album covers.
![../../_images/cover-flow.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cover-flow.gif)
To set the content and behavior of the Cover Flow, in the Node Tree or Prefabs select the Cover Flow > Scene> Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties add and set:
  * Items Source to provide a data source for the list items.
  * Selection Behavior to set whether the list box brings an item to the center of the list box area when the user selects that item.

![../../_images/items-source-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/items-source-property.png) ![../../_images/selection-behavior-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior-property.png)
###  Poster Flow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#poster-flow "Link to this heading")
Use the Poster Flow to present media posters.
![../../_images/poster-flow.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/poster-flow.gif)
To adjust the roundness of poster corners, in the Prefabs select the Poster prefab and in the Properties set the Rounding Radius property.
![../../_images/poster-flow-rounding-radius.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/poster-flow-rounding-radius.png)
To set the content and behavior of the Poster Flow, in the Node Tree or Prefabs select the Poster Flow > Scene> Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties add and set:
  * Items Source to provide a data source for the list items.

## Complete user interface components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#complete-user-interface-components "Link to this heading")
Factory Content includes complete user interface components that you can use to add functionality to your application.
###  Car[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#car "Link to this heading")
Use the Car to add a car model.
![../../_images/car-asset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-asset.png)
To position the car, in the Preview use either the Node tool or the Camera tool. See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html) and [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).
To set the material for the different parts of the car, you can drag materials from the Assets window to the Car in the Preview window. See [Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html).
###  Music Player[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#music-player "Link to this heading")
Use the Music Player to create a music player with buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/music-player.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/music-player.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the Music Player buttons react to user input. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
###  Navigation Bar[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#navigation-bar "Link to this heading")
Use the Navigation Bar to create a navigation bar with toggle buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/navigation-bar.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-bar.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the Navigation Bar buttons react to user input. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html)
###  Notification Popup[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#notification-popup "Link to this heading")
Use the Notification Popup to create a notification dialog with buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/notification-popup.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/notification-popup.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the Notification Popup buttons react to user input. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
###  Traditional Gauges[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#traditional-gauges "Link to this heading")
Use the Traditional Gauges to create a car cluster with speed, RPM, fuel, and temperature gauges.
![../../_images/traditional-gauges.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/traditional-gauges.gif)
To control the visibility of the speed and RPM gauges, in the Properties add and set the Gauge State property.
To move the indicators, in the Properties add and set:
  * Fuel to move the fuel indicator.
  * RPM to move the RPM indicator.
  * Speed to move the speed indicator.
  * Temperature to move the temperature indicator.

![../../_images/gauges-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/gauges-properties.png)

Rubber Material

## Render Passes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#render-passes "Link to this heading")
Factory Content includes render passes that you can use to add effects to your project.
###  Skybox render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#skybox-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Use the Skybox render pass to draw a Cubemap as a background into your Scene.
![../../_images/skybox-asset.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/skybox-asset.gif)
To set up the Skybox render pass
  * In Asset Packages > Factory Content, right-click Skybox and select Import to bring the package as a prefab in to the Library > Render Pass Prefabs folder.
  * If you do not have a custom Render Pass Prefab selected in your Viewport 2D, in Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs, right-click and Create > Default render pass. In the Properties of your Viewport 2D, set the Default render pass as the value of the Render Pass Prefab property.
  * In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs, drag the Skybox render pass from its root node under the Draw Objects Opaque node of the Render Pass Prefab assigned to the target Viewport 2D.
  * To adjust the Skybox background, select and adjust the properties on the Skybox Render Pass View in the previous step.
    * To adjust the color of the background, adjust the CubemapColor property.
    * To select the background cubemap texture, use the TextureCube property.
    * To override the tracking camera, use the Override Camera property.
    * To adjust the orientation of the background, use the Skybox Orientation property.

![../../_images/skybox-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/skybox-properties.png)

sub_documents.title: Filters
sub_documents.summary: This page describes filters in Kanzi, which collect and reorganize 3D nodes for rendering. Filters are used in render passes to determine which nodes to render, such as in Draw Objects, Draw Objects With Material, or Node List render passes. Available filters include Contains Property Filter, Object Type Filter, Property Is Equal Filter, Sorting Filter, and Tag Filter. The page also mentions using filters in the API via the FilterObjectSource class and provides links to related tutorials and best practices.

# Filters[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/filters.html#filters "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Filters collect and reorganize 3D nodes in your Kanzi project. You can use filters to determine which 3D nodes to render in different render passes.
After you set one or more filters or object sources, a filter collects and outputs a set of 3D nodes that match the requirements you define in that filter.
Use filters to adjust the rendering for the whole or parts of your Kanzi application. To use a filter, either:
  * In a Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass set the Object Source property so that the render pass renders only those nodes that the filter passes to the render pass.
  * In a Node List render pass set the Filter property so that the Node List render pass holds only those nodes that the filter passes to that Node List render pass.
Use a Node List render pass when you want to filter anything but the 3D nodes that you want to render, such as Light nodes. Draw Objects render pass, Draw Objects With Material render pass, and Gather Lights render passes can use the result node list of the same Node List render pass.


See [Rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html).
For example, you can use filters to:
  * Create reflections for nodes. See [Tutorial: Create reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/reflections/reflections.html).
  * Apply a stencil to 3D content. See [Tutorial: Apply a stencil to 3D content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/stencil/stencil.html).
  * Distribute rendering across several frames. See [Tutorial: Progressive rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/progressive-rendering/progressive-rendering.html).
  * Render only transparent nodes. See [Rendering partially transparent nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/rendering-transparent-objects.html).


These filters are available in Kanzi Studio in the Library > Rendering > Object Sources:
  * Contains Property Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property.
See [Using the Contains Property Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-contains-property-filters.html).
  * Object Type Filter collects 3D nodes based on their type. See [Using the Object Type Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-object-type-filters.html).
  * Property Is Equal Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property the value of which matches a specific value.
See [Using the Property Is Equal Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-property-is-equal-filters.html).
  * Sorting Filter either orders 3D nodes by their position on the z axis or groups them by their material type.
See [Using the Sorting Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-sorting-filters.html).
  * Tag Filter collects 3D nodes that have a specific tag assigned.
See [Using the Tag Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-tag-filters.html).

![../../_images/create-filters.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-filters.png)
## Using filters in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/filters.html#using-filters-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `FilterObjectSource[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a12710.html)` class.
