With Kanzi plugins, you can extend the functionality of Kanzi and customize Kanzi to fit your application development requirements. When you create a Kanzi plugin, you can share the extended functionality with any Kanzi user.
In Kanzi you can create and use these types of plugins:
  * Kanzi Studio plugins extend the functionality of Kanzi Studio and run in Kanzi Studio.
For Kanzi Studio you can create:
    * Kanzi Studio command plugins are plugins that you execute as commands and do not have a user interface. For example, use the command plugins to execute a command on the entire or the selected part of the node tree in your project.
See [Creating Kanzi Studio command plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-studio-plugins.html).
    * Kanzi Studio window plugins are plugins that you use in a Kanzi Studio window and have a user interface. For example, use the window plugins to create an editor or to visualize the content in your project.
See [Creating Kanzi Studio window plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-studio-window-plugins.html).
  * Kanzi Engine plugins extend the functionality of Kanzi Engine. Kanzi Engine executes these plugins on target platforms.
See [Creating Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-engine-plugins.html).


Kanzi Studio plugins extend the functionality of Kanzi Studio and run in Kanzi Studio.
For example, you can extend the functionality of Kanzi Studio to:
  * Automate tasks that take a lot of time to do manually in Kanzi Studio, or are prone to errors.
  * Import and export content from Kanzi Studio, such as localization tables in a format that Kanzi Studio does not support
  * Create editors that abstract the details and speed up the workflow, such as visualization tools that support work on your projects in Kanzi Studio.


## Kanzi Studio data model[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/plugins.html#ks-data-model "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Studio project is a hierarchical structure of project nodes. Each node has a set of properties and can have a set of child nodes or items. Different types of project items, such as nodes, models, textures, and animations have their own characteristics. For example, textures specify the image used in the texture and filtering. To change the data in the project Kanzi Studio uses commands. For example, set values to properties, or create new items.
Kanzi Studio provides the `KanziStudio[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html)` object to plugins. The `KanziStudio[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html)` object is the root object for data access and provides the current project, available commands, global undo and redo, and events related to project opening and closing.
You can access the nodes, resources, and properties in the project using the current project node. Use libraries for different types of nodes and factory for new project nodes and resources. Nodes provide the access to properties, child nodes and items, changes in the current node and descendants, and events.

sub_documents.title: Using node prefabs
sub_documents.summary: This page explains how to use node prefabs in Kanzi Studio to create reusable UI components, instantiate them via Prefab Placeholder or Prefab View nodes, customize instances by overriding properties, edit prefabs, convert existing nodes into prefabs, and asynchronously load prefab resources to keep the application responsive. It also covers memory considerations and best practices for using prefabs.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Using node prefabs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#using-node-prefabs "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use prefabs (prefabricated templates) to structure your application and to create consistent interfaces. Prefabs allow you to create the building blocks of your application and make the application easier to maintain.
Create a prefab for every item in your application that appears more than once, when you want to logically separate a part of your application, or add content to the node tree when your application is already running. For example, use prefabs to:
  * Create content with consistent structure. For example, with prefabs you can create buttons that always have the same structure, but can vary in appearance.
  * Modularize your project and make it easier to maintain.
  * Control the loading and launch times of your Kanzi application.
  * Create different themes for your Kanzi application.
  * Localize your Kanzi application.


When using prefabs keep in mind that:
  * You can duplicate an instance of a prefab like any other node in the node tree.
  * Property values you add to an instance of a prefab override the property values set in the prefab.
  * Use relative paths when you want to reference items inside a prefab (for example, in a message trigger or a property binding). Do not use the prefab itself as a target path for any messages or animations.


You can nest prefabs within prefabs.
## Node prefabs and node prefab instances[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#node-prefabs-and-node-prefab-instances "Link to this heading")
Node prefabs consume memory on the device only when you load them. When you load a node prefab, the prefab consumes the amount of memory based on the number of nodes and properties that prefab contains. When you instantiate a node prefab, Kanzi creates nodes and assigns properties to those nodes. You can calculate how much memory prefab instances consume by multiplying the number of instances with the memory requirements of a single prefab instance.
When you attach a node to the node tree, resources used by the nodes are looked up and requested from the resource manager. Resource manager loads or returns existing resources if they are already loaded.
When you detach a node prefab instance, Kanzi does not release resources used in the nodes you detached. This is a performance optimization, which allows you to change the parent node of the prefab, or move a prefab in the node tree, without having to load again the resources the prefab uses. When you want to release all resources which are no longer in use, call `ResourceManager::purge[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13998.html#ada106a4cfa891d8cbe13f104db826f85)`.
Kanzi assumes that all the nodes that you place in the node tree are going to be used. Kanzi optimizes for the case that all the content put in the node tree is ready for immediate use. If a node is not supposed to be used, remove it from the node tree.
##  Prefab Placeholder and Prefab View nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#prefab-placeholder-and-prefab-view-nodes "Link to this heading")
You can use both Prefab Placeholder and Prefab View nodes to instantiate a node prefab in your project. The difference between these nodes is:
  * When you instantiate a node prefab with a Prefab Placeholder node, Kanzi reads the value of the Prefab Template property once and replaces the Prefab Placeholder node with the prefab to which that property points.
For example, if you use a Prefab Placeholder 2D node to instantiate a node prefab which contains a Button 2D node, when Kanzi instantiates the node prefab, it replaces the Prefab Placeholder 2D node with the root node of the Button 2D prefab.
  * When you instantiate a node prefab with a Prefab View node, Kanzi monitors the value of the Prefab Template property and adds the prefab to which that property points as a child node of the Prefab View node. This allows you to change the prefab that the Prefab View instantiates and to keep your application responsive when it is loading resources. See [Loading node prefab resources asynchronously](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#loading-node-prefab-resources-asynchronously).
For example, if you use a Prefab View 2D node to instantiate a node prefab which contains a Button 2D node, when Kanzi instantiates the prefab, it adds the root node of the Button 2D node as a child node of the Prefab View 2D node.


### When to use a Prefab Placeholder and when a Prefab View node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#when-to-use-a-prefab-placeholder-and-when-a-prefab-view-node "Link to this heading")
Use a Prefab Placeholder node to instantiate a node prefab which you do not intend to change during application runtime.
If you want to dynamically change a prefab, or want to asynchronously load the resources which the prefab uses, use a Prefab View to instantiate a prefab. For example, when you theme your application and want to use different prefabs for different themes, use a Prefab View node to instantiate those prefabs.
Kanzi reads the value of the Prefab Template property of a Prefab Placeholder once, but a Prefab View node monitors for changes the value of the Prefab Template property. When the value of the Prefab Template property in a Prefab View changes, Kanzi replaces its child node with the new child node.
## Creating and using a node prefab[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#creating-and-using-a-node-prefab "Link to this heading")
To create and use a node prefab:
  1. In the Prefabs click ![create-prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-prefab.png) and select the prefab you want to create.
For example, create a Button 2D prefab, and add an Image and a Text Block 2D node to it.
![../../_images/reuse-create-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-create-prefab.png)
  2. To instantiate the prefab in your application:
     * From the Prefabs drag the prefab you created to the Node Tree and drop it on the node where you want to use that prefab.
Kanzi Studio creates a Prefab Placeholder node which instantiates the prefab in your project.
![../../_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/button-prefab-placeholder-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-prefab-placeholder-in-project.png)
To instantiate a different prefab, in the Node Tree select the prefab you want to change, and in the Properties set the Prefab Template property to the prefab you want to instantiate.
![../../_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-properties.png)
     * In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to instantiate the prefab, select Prefab View, and in the Properties set the Prefab Template property to the prefab you want to instantiate.
![../../_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-prefab-view.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-prefab-view.png) ![../../_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-prefab-view-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-prefab-view-properties.png)


## Customizing instances of a node prefab[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-a-node-prefab "Link to this heading")
A node prefab can contain a tree of nodes, each with their own properties. When you edit the nodes in a prefab or any of its instances in a project, you change those nodes in all instances of that prefab. You can customize each instance of a prefab to have its own property values by overriding the property values of the prefab. For example, when you create a prefab for an address book entry, you want to show a different name, number, and photo for each address book entry.
To customize instances of a node prefab:
  1. In the Prefabs select the node in a prefab that you want to customize in an instance of that prefab.
For example, to use a different texture for each instance of a prefab, select an Image node.
![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-structure.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-structure.png)
  2. In the Properties, next to the property that you want to customize, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png).
Kanzi Studio creates from that property a custom property, adds it to the root node of that prefab, and creates a `##Template` binding to the property in the root node of that prefab.
See [Prefab root bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#prefab-root-bindings).
For example, to customize the texture that you want to show in different instances of that prefab, click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png) next to the Image property. Kanzi Studio creates a custom Image property, adds it to the root node of that node prefab, and creates in the Image node a `##Template` binding to the custom Image property in the root node of that node prefab.
![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-publish.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-publish.png) ![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-root-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-root-binding.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the root node of the prefab instance that you want to customize.
![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-prefab-instance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-prefab-instance.png)
  4. In the Properties click ![image2](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-property.png) next to the property that you customized and set the value of the property.
Only this instance of the prefab uses the value that you set.
![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-add-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-add-property.png) ![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-property-added.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-property-added.png)


## Editing a node prefab[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#editing-a-node-prefab "Link to this heading")
To edit a node prefab double-click the prefab in the Prefabs. Kanzi Studio shows only the prefab in a Preview window tab. You can now edit the prefab with the Preview tools and see the result of your edits without instantiating the prefab.
![../../_images/reuse-composition.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-composition.png)
## Turning nodes into prefab[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#turning-nodes-into-prefab "Link to this heading")
To turn any part of the node tree of your project into a prefab, from the Node Tree drag the root of the part you want to turn into a prefab to the Prefabs.
![../../_images/creating-a-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/creating-a-prefab.png)
When you drop a node into the Prefabs window, Kanzi Studio creates a prefab template from the node and replaces the original node with an instance of the prefab.
![../../_images/creating-a-prefab---prefab-in-the-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/creating-a-prefab---prefab-in-the-prefabs.png)
## Loading node prefab resources asynchronously[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#loading-node-prefab-resources-asynchronously "Link to this heading")
When you load prefab resources asynchronously, Kanzi uses separate threads to load resources. When Kanzi finishes loading the resources, it deploys them using the main thread. That way your application stays responsive while it loads resources. To load resources asynchronously from several prefabs, see [Tutorial: Load and deploy resources asynchronously](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/loading/loading.html).
Use resource profiling to measure during runtime how long it takes to load and deploy resources and prefabs in your Kanzi application.
Resource profiling data helps you find out which resources to load asynchronously.
See [Measuring the loading and deployment time of resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/performance-profiling/resource-profiling.html).
To load node prefab resources asynchronously:
  1. Create the content that you want to show while Kanzi loads resources of a node prefab.
For example, to create a loading screen that you replace with the content of a prefab whose resources you load asynchronously, from the Asset Packages > Factory Content drag the Processing Indicator and drop it on the Prefabs window.
![../../_images/processing-indicator-asset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator-asset.png) ![../../_images/processing-indicator-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator-project.png)
  2. Create a node prefab whose resources you want to load asynchronously.
For example, in the Prefabs create a Stack Layout 2D and add to it several Image nodes each of which points to a different image.
![../../_images/async-load-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/async-load-content.png)
  3. In the Node Tree, create a Prefab View node where you want to asynchronously load prefab resources. In the Properties, set the Prefab Template property to the content that you want to show while Kanzi loads the resources of the prefab that you created in the previous step.
For example, set the Prefab Template property to the Processing Indicator prefab.
![../../_images/prefab-view-2d-processing-indicator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-view-2d-processing-indicator.png) ![../../_images/prefab-view-2d-displayed-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-view-2d-displayed-prefab.png)
  4. In the Node Tree, select the Prefab View node. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click Triggers and select the trigger that you want to use to start loading prefab resources.
For example, add the On Attached trigger to start loading resources when Kanzi attaches the Prefab View node to the screen graph.
![../../_images/add-on-attached.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-on-attached.png)
  5. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you added in the previous step, and select Dispatch Message Action > Prefab View > Start Asynchronous Load.
![../../_images/on-attached-trigger-start-async-load-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/on-attached-trigger-start-async-load-action.png)
  6. In the Start Asynchronous Load action, set the Prefab Template property to a prefab or a resource ID that points to a prefab whose resources you want to load asynchronously.
![../../_images/start-async-load-action-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/start-async-load-action-settings.png)
  7. To define what happens when Kanzi finishes loading the resources:
    1. In the Node Tree, select the Prefab View node. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click Triggers and select Message Trigger > Prefab View > Asynchronous Load Completed.
![../../_images/prefab-view-2d-processing-indicator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-view-2d-processing-indicator.png) ![../../_images/add-asynchronous-load-completed-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-asynchronous-load-completed-trigger.png)
    2. In the Node Components > Triggers, press `Alt` and right-click the Asynchronous Load Completed trigger and select an action.
For example, select the Dispatch Message Action > Activity Host > Activate Activity action and set:
       * Target Item to the Activity Host node that contains the Activity that you want to activate
       * Activity Activation Path to the Activity that you want to activate when Kanzi finishes loading the resources
![../../_images/asynchronous-load-completed-add-navigate-to-page-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asynchronous-load-completed-add-navigate-to-page-action.png) ![../../_images/navigation-request-for-asynchronous-load-completed.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-request-for-asynchronous-load-completed.png)
  8. Select File > Export > Export as KZB Player for Windows and open the application exe file in the `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Application Player` directory.
Because the Kanzi Studio Preview loads all resources in the project when it starts, to see the effect of loading resources asynchronously, either:
     * Export the project as a kzb file Player
     * Export the project kzb file and run the application from the project Visual Studio solution
![../../_images/export-as-kzb-player-for-windows.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-as-kzb-player-for-windows.png)


## Replacing the root node of a node prefab[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#replacing-the-root-node-of-a-node-prefab "Link to this heading")
Replace the root node of a prefab when you want to add or change the node that is used as the parent node of a prefab. For example, if you first created a prefab that has a Grid Layout 3D as its root, but now you want to place that Grid Layout 3D into a Stack Layout 3D, you need to replace the root node of that prefab.
To replace the root of a node prefab:
  1. In the Prefabs press `Alt` and right-click the root of the prefab you want to replace and select Empty Node From Items.
Kanzi Studio replaces the current root of the prefab with an Empty Node node and places the entire prefab inside that empty node. For 3D prefabs Kanzi Studio creates an Empty Node 3D node, for 2D prefabs it creates an Empty Node 2D node.
![../../_images/change-root-of-prefab---before.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/change-root-of-prefab---before.png) ![../../_images/change-root-of-prefab---empty-node-root.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/change-root-of-prefab---empty-node-root.png)
  2. In the Prefabs create the node you want to use as the new root node of the prefab.
For example, create a Stack Layout 3D.
![../../_images/change-root-of-prefab---new-root-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/change-root-of-prefab---new-root-node.png)
  3. Drag and drop the old prefab from the Empty Node node root to the new root node you created in the previous step.
![../../_images/change-root-of-prefab---after.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/change-root-of-prefab---after.png)


## Using the Prefab View 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#using-the-prefab-view-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To use a Prefab view 3D node, create a prefab with 3D content and set it using setPrefab():

```
// Create a Prefab view 3D and add it to the scene.
PrefabView3DSharedPtr prefabView3D = PrefabView3D::create(domain, "Prefab view");
scene->addChild(prefabView3D);

// Acquire prefab from resource manager.
PrefabTemplateSharedPtr prefabTemplate = resourceManager->acquireResource<PrefabTemplate>("kzb://my_project/Prefabs/My3DPrefab");

// Use the prefab in the PrefabView3D node.
prefabView3D->setPrefab(prefabTemplate);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `PrefabView3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18798.html)` class.
## Using the Prefab View 2D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#using-the-prefab-view-2d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To use a Prefab View 2D node, create a prefab with 2D content and set it using setPrefab():

```
// Create a Prefab view 2D and add it to the viewport.
PrefabView2DSharedPtr prefabView2D = PrefabView2D::create(domain, "Prefab view");
viewportNode->addChild(prefabView2D);

// Acquire prefab from resource manager.
PrefabTemplateSharedPtr prefabTemplate = resourceManager->acquireResource<PrefabTemplate>("kzb://my_project/Prefabs/My2DPrefab");

// Use the prefab in the PrefabView2D node.
prefabView2D->setPrefab(prefabTemplate);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `PrefabView2D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18794.html)` class.
##  Prefab View property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#prefab-view-property-types "Link to this heading")
For lists of the available property types for the Prefab View nodes, see [Prefab View 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/prefab-view-2d-reference.html) and [Prefab View 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/prefab-view-3d-reference.html).
##  Prefab Placeholder property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#prefab-placeholder-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For lists of the available property types and messages for the Prefab Placeholder nodes, see [Prefab Placeholder 2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/prefab-placeholder-2d-reference.html) and [Prefab Placeholder 3D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/prefab-placeholder-3d-reference.html).
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html)

[Tutorial: Load and deploy resources asynchronously](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/loading/loading.html)

sub_documents.title: Preview
sub_documents.summary: This page introduces the Preview feature in Kanzi Studio, which displays real-time changes made to a Kanzi application. It covers the standard Preview window, the Target Preview for viewing on actual devices, and mentions capabilities like controlling, editing, and analyzing performance in the Preview. It also includes notes about firewall settings, handling large content with out-of-memory errors, and links to related documentation.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/preview.html#preview "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Kanzi shows in real-time the changes that you make in your Kanzi Studio project:
  * The Preview window shows the content of the currently open Kanzi application. For example, the Preview in this image shows the Kanzi application you can create by completing the [Tutorial: Create gauges](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/gauges/gauges.html).
![../../_images/start4.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/start4.png)
Note
The Kanzi Studio Preview by default uses the TCP/IP for internal communication with Kanzi Studio. If you have a firewall installed on your computer, allow the `Kanzi Preview` process to go through the firewall.
Tip
When you are working with large content, such as 4K textures, the Preview cannot process the data in-memory and can terminate during startup with an out-of-memory error. To enable the Preview to start, in Edit > User Preferences > Advanced tab enable the Export initial Preview data to hard drive setting.
You can estimate whether enabling this setting is necessary by exporting the kzb file of your project. If the size of the kzb file is larger than 300 MB, enable the setting.
By enabling this setting, the Preview loads the initial data to the hard drive, instead of the memory. Enable this setting only when your are working with Kanzi Studio projects where the memory transfer exceeds the 32-bit memory limit of the Preview. When this setting is enabled, the Preview takes longer time to load your projects and start because a hard drive is slower than memory.
  * The Target Preview enables you to see on a target device the changes that you make in a Kanzi Studio project without exporting and redeploying the application.
These are the impacts of Target Preview on development workflow:
    * It shows your application as it is, including the rendering and latency, and any behavior that you define in platform-specific code. The content that the Target Preview shows is not a video stream.
    * The Target Preview enables you to revise your design even in late stages of the development. You can instantly test designs and see how your changes look in a real environment, such as on a display inside a vehicle.
    * When you develop an Android application using the Kanzi Android framework (droidfw), you can see full composited application that consists of both Kanzi and Android UI.
See [Target Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-target-preview.html).
![../../_images/target-preview-android.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-preview-android.gif)


In the Kanzi Studio Preview you can:
  * Control what the Preview shows. See [Controlling the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html).
  * Create and position 2D nodes, create and edit Text Block nodes, add triggers, create and position Camera nodes, and zoom and pan around the Preview.
See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html).
  * Analyze the performance of your application. See [Analyzing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html).


By default the Preview shows your application using the default Kanzi Studio Preview application.
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/preview.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Controlling the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html)

sub_documents.title: Prism graphs
sub_documents.summary: This page introduces Prism graphs, a visual node-based editor in Kanzi for creating render graphs. It covers graph presets (Default, Empty, Offscreen Buffer), editor navigation shortcuts, common editing operations (creating/deleting nodes, connecting/disconnecting, adding/removing properties, binding properties), and the minimap feature. It also provides links to related tutorials on creating graphs, bloom effects, shadows, and property bindings.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Prism graphs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#prism-graphs "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Prism graph editor is a visual node tool for creating render graphs. You can add or remove rendering nodes and quickly iterate on visual effects. Graphs provide a clear overview of rendering operations, let you adjust properties, and show results instantly.
Prism simplifies rendering complexities into a handful of basic primitive operations. A typical graph consists of one or more draw operations, shadow rendering operations, and post-processing effect compositions.
A Prism graph consists of nodes such as Draw, Blit, Clear and other more advanced nodes. Nodes are linked together using connections to form a render pipeline, where each operation runs according to the graph structure. Every graph has an output node that displays the final result on screen.
See [Creating Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html) for a walkthrough on creating a Prism graph.
## Prism graph presets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#prism-graph-presets "Link to this heading")
Prism offers quick presets to get started when you create a new graph. You can find the available presets when you create a new graph. Go to **Library** > **Prism Graphs** , right-click on **Prism Graphs** , and select **Create** > **Template**.
![../../_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png)
### Default Prism Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#default-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/default-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/default-graph.png)
A preset configuration for a render graph similar to Kanzi’s default render pass. The preset draws opaque and transparent objects.
This is a good general starting point to start customizing your rendering.
### Empty Prism Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#empty-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/empty-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/empty-graph.png)
Empty Prism graph only has an output node. By default, this graph doesn’t render anything.
### Offscreen Buffer Prism Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#offscreen-buffer-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/offscreen-framebuffer-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/offscreen-framebuffer-graph.png)
A preset tailored for quickly starting with offscreen or post-processing effects. The graph renders objects to screen and then composites a full-screen shader using blit nodes.
This is a good starting point for building post-processing or offscreen rendering effects where you want to apply a shader to all pixels on screen.
## Navigating the Prism editor[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#navigating-the-prism-editor "Link to this heading")  
| Action  | Shortcut  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Select  | Left-click a node or connection  |  
| Pan  | Middle mouse button  |  
| Zoom  | Mouse wheel  |  
## Working with Prism graphs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#working-with-prism-graphs "Link to this heading")
Here are the most common operations for editing Prism graphs.
### Creating nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#creating-nodes "Link to this heading")
**Right-click** in the graph and select a node type.
![../../_images/creating-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/creating-prism-nodes.gif)
### Deleting nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#deleting-nodes "Link to this heading")
Select a node and press `Delete`.
Or **right-click** and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/deleting-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/deleting-nodes.gif)
### Connecting nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#connecting-nodes "Link to this heading")
Drag from a socket with the **left mouse button**. Release on a valid socket to connect.
![../../_images/connecting-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/connecting-prism-nodes.gif)
### Disconnecting nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#disconnecting-nodes "Link to this heading")
Select a connection and press `Delete`.
Or right-click and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/disconnecting-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/disconnecting-prism-nodes.gif)
To delete multiple connections, hold `Shift` + `Alt` and draw a line over the connections.
![../../_images/disconnecting-multiple-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/disconnecting-multiple-prism-nodes.gif)
### Adding properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#adding-properties "Link to this heading")
Click the **+** icon on a node and select a property.
![../../_images/adding-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adding-properties.gif)
You can add multiple properties by clicking a property category.
![../../_images/adding-multiple-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adding-multiple-properties.gif)
Tip
Each Viewport that shares a Prism graph can override individual material property values independently. Select a property on a Prism node and click the Override value from Viewport button to set a per-Viewport value without affecting other Viewports that use the same graph.
![../../_images/prism-override-property.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prism-override-property.gif)
### Removing properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#removing-properties "Link to this heading")
Right-click a property and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/deleting-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/deleting-properties.gif)
### Adding and removing properties on a Render Pass node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#adding-and-removing-properties-on-a-render-pass-node "Link to this heading")
On a **Render Pass** node, click ![add-properties-window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png) to open the Add Properties window. Use the window to add or remove any property the render pass supports.
### Binding Render Pass node properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#binding-render-pass-node-properties "Link to this heading")
You can bind a property on a Render Pass node so its value is driven by another property or by a binding expression. The following types of property bindings are supported:
  * **Resource property bindings.** Drag a binding line directly between two resource properties of the same type.
![Animation of dragging a binding line between two resource properties on different Prism nodes.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bind-toplevelas.gif)
  * **Text property bindings.** Right-click a non-resource property row and select Edit binding… to drive the property from a binding expression. The row then shows a binding indicator and a read-only preview of the expression.
![A Prism property row showing a binding indicator on the label and a read-only expression preview in place of the value editor.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clear-color-bound-row.gif)


See [Binding Render Pass node properties](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html) for worked examples.
### Minimap[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#minimap "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/minimap.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/minimap.png)
![minimap_icon](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/minimap-toggle.png)
You can enable the minimap from the top-left corner of the Prism editor.
The minimap shows an overview of your graph. A light rectangle shows the visible area in the Prism Editor. Use the minimap to navigate large graphs.  
| Action  | Shortcut  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Resize  | Drag the lower-left corner of the minimap  |  
| Zoom  | Scroll the mouse wheel  |  
| Center view  | Click in the minimap  |  
| Pan  | Drag in the minimap  |

sub_documents.title: Projects
sub_documents.summary: This page describes Kanzi Studio projects, including their structure, directory layout, and key concepts. It explains that Kanzi applications use kzb files as source content, projects can be combined, and each project consists of objects and resources with parent-child relationships. The project directory contains project files (.proj.kzm), backups, lock files, and resource directories. It also mentions restore points and provides links to related topics.

# Projects[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/projects.html#projects "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Kanzi applications use kzb Kanzi files as the source of application content and event logic.
You can use one or more Kanzi Studio projects to create your Kanzi application.
See [Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html).
You can configure your project in Kanzi Studio by selecting Project > Properties.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png)
In Kanzi Studio you can have only one project open at a time.
## Kanzi Studio project structure[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/projects.html#ks-project-structure "Link to this heading")
Your Kanzi Studio project consists of project objects and resources. Each object in the project has a parent, a name, and a set of properties that define it. Additionally, most objects have either child or item objects.
In addition to the parent link and the child links in the children collection, items can also refer to other branches in the project tree. For example, animation objects have animation library as their parent but have a list of references to animation that act as their child nodes. This allows animation instancing where several animation nodes can share a single child node in their child node lists.
## Project directory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/projects.html#project-directory "Link to this heading")
By default, Kanzi Studio projects are stored in the `<KanziWorkspace>/Projects` directory. For every project Kanzi Studio creates a directory that contains:
  * **Project files**. Kanzi Studio stores the project data in kzm files. The root project file has the `.proj.kzm` extension. While you can manually modify the project files, they are designed to be modified only by Kanzi Studio.
  * **Project file backups**. When you save your project, Kanzi Studio makes a copy of the project file and stores it in a file with the `.proj.kzm_N` extension, where N is the consecutive number of the backup.
  * **Project file lock**. When you open a project, Kanzi Studio creates a lock file in the project directory. The project lock file prevents the opening of more than one copy of a project. Kanzi Studio deletes the project lock file when you close the project.
  * **Resource file directories**. These directories contain files that are part of a Kanzi Studio project but their contents are not included in the project file. For example, this includes image files and shader source files.
You can access most of the contents of the resource file directories in Kanzi Studio in Library > Resource Files. When you add a file to any of these directories in the file system, that file is automatically added to the Library, with the following exceptions:
    * Mesh Data and Animations directories are used only by Kanzi Studio. The files in these directories contain the vertex and index data of the meshes and animation keyframe data of the animations. If you are using source control system, remember to add these files to the source control whenever you import meshes or create new animations in your Kanzi Studio project.
    * Source Assets directory is a storage place for the native files where you can store image processing applications and digital content creation tools so that they remain with the project. Kanzi Studio does not handle these files and does not export them into the kzb file of your Kanzi application. You cannot access the Source Assets directory from the Kanzi Studio.
  * Restore Points directory. Use restore points to return to an earlier version of your project. When you create a restore point for a project, Kanzi Studio makes the complete copy of your project into a timestamped directory in the `<ProjectName>/Restore Points` directory. See [Creating restore points](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/backups/backups.html#creating-restore-points).


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/projects.html#sa "Link to this heading")

sub_documents.title: Property types
sub_documents.summary: This page introduces property types in Kanzi, which define the name, category, and data type of properties used to specify and examine node state, appearance, and behavior. It explains that properties provide a uniform way to access node data, enabling animation, bindings, and monitoring of value changes. The page also mentions how to create custom property types in Kanzi Studio or Kanzi Engine plugins, and provides links to related documentation on using properties, the property system, and the property types reference.

# Property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/property-types.html#property-types "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Properties provide the means to specify and examine the state, appearance, and behavior of nodes. For example, a property can define a color, indicate whether a button is pressed, or specify the alignment of an item.
Properties provide a uniform way to access data of Kanzi nodes, so that many Kanzi subsystems can manipulate the data. That way you can, for example, animate property values, provide bindings between property values, and monitor property value changes.
Each property in Kanzi is described by a property type. The property type describes the name and category of the property and type of data and values the property can have.
You can create custom property types to support the logic of your Kanzi application:
  * In Kanzi Studio. See [Creating property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/creating-custom-property-types.html).
  * In a Kanzi Engine plugin. See [Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/plugins-kanzi-engine.html).


To learn how to work with properties in Kanzi Studio, see [Using properties in Kanzi Studio](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/using-properties.html).
To learn about how the Kanzi property system works, see [Property system](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/property-system.html).
For a list of default property types, see [Property types reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/property-types-reference.html).

sub_documents.title: Rendering
sub_documents.summary: This page from Kanzi documentation explains the rendering system in Kanzi Studio, focusing on render passes. It describes how render passes define the rendering of 3D content, including camera, nodes, lights, materials, composition targets, and post-processing effects. It lists various render pass types (Blit, Clear, Composition Target, Cubemap, Draw Objects, Draw Objects With Material, Gather Lights, Group, Material Setup, Node List, Pipeline State) and render pass presets (Compose and Blit Pass, Default render pass, Render to Texture Pass, Image-Based Lighting Filter Pass). It also provides links to related topics such as best practices, using render passes, lights, node collection, composition targets, materials, post-processing, cubemap reflections, object sources, filters, culling, and tutorials.

# Rendering[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#rendering "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use render passes to define the rendering of 3D content in your Kanzi application.
For example, in render passes you can define:
  * Which Camera that render pass and its descendants use for rendering. See [Setting the camera for render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html#setting-the-camera-for-render-passes).
  * What nodes the render pass renders. See [Collecting nodes for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/filtering-node-lists.html).
  * What lights to use to light the content. See [Using lights in rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/lights-rendering.html).
  * What material to use to render the content. [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html).
  * The format of the composition target. See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html).
  * Post-processing effects. [Creating a post-processing effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/post-processing-grayscale.html).


In a render pass prefab, you can create a hierarchy of render passes to achieve a specific rendering result.
In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs each top-level render pass is the root of a render pass prefab.
Kanzi executes the render passes in each render pass prefab from top to bottom the way they appear in the render pass prefab in the Library. Each render pass applies its settings and renders its children. See [Using render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html).
For example, the Default render pass, which is one of the render pass presets that come with Kanzi Studio, creates a basic set of render passes that first render opaque nodes and then transparent nodes. See [Using the Default render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#using-drp).
![../../_images/rendering.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rendering.svg)
## Render passes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#render-passes "Link to this heading")
These render passes are available in Kanzi:
###  Blit render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#blit-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Blit render pass blits one or more single textures or cubemap textures on the screen using a specific material.
See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html), [Rendering multiple render passes or textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-multiple.html), and [Creating a post-processing effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/post-processing-grayscale.html).
![../../_images/blit-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blit-render-pass.svg)
###  Clear render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#clear-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Clear render pass clears some or all of the buffers of the current render context.
You can set the values to which Kanzi clears the color, depth, and stencil buffer.
![../../_images/clear-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clear-render-pass.svg)
###  Composition Target render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#composition-target-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Composition Target render pass renders itself and its descendant render passes to one or more composition targets.
See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html).
![../../_images/composition-target-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/composition-target-render-pass.svg)
###  Cubemap render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#cubemap-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Cubemap render pass renders itself and its child render passes to an active composition target, such as a Cubemap Render Target Texture and the Result Texture of the Cubemap render pass.
See [Creating cubemap reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/cubemap-render-pass.html).
![../../_images/cubemap-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cubemap-render-pass.svg)![../../_images/preview-cubemap-reflections.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-cubemap-reflections.gif)
###  Draw Objects render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#draw-objects-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Draw Objects render pass allows you to set a Camera node to render a specific list of nodes using specific light nodes.
The Draw Objects render pass:
  * By default uses the default Camera node to render all nodes in a Scene node, or the nodes passed to it by its nearest ancestor Node List render pass. See [Setting the camera for render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html#setting-the-camera-for-render-passes) and [Collecting nodes for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/filtering-node-lists.html).
  * By default renders nodes using the light nodes provided by its nearest ancestor Gather Lights render pass. See [Using lights in rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/lights-rendering.html).
  * Uses the rendering parameters that you set in its nearest ancestor Pipeline State render pass.
  * Allows you to control frustum culling. See [Controlling frustum culling](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/meshes/setting-culling.html#controlling-frustum-culling).

![../../_images/draw-objects-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-render-pass.svg)![../../_images/draw-objects-render-pass-example.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-render-pass-example.svg)
###  Draw Objects With Material render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#draw-objects-with-material-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Draw Objects With Material render pass works like a Draw Objects render pass but allows you to set a material that it uses to render content. See [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html).
![../../_images/draw-objects-with-material-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-with-material-render-pass.svg)![../../_images/draw-objects-with-material-render-example.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-objects-with-material-render-example.svg)
###  Gather Lights render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#gather-lights-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Gather Lights render pass allows you to collect from a list of nodes the light nodes for lighting 3D nodes in a scene.
See [Using lights in rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/lights-rendering.html).
![../../_images/gather-lights-render-pass1.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/gather-lights-render-pass1.svg)
###  Group render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#group-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Group render pass allows you to collect render passes so that you can refer to a single render pass prefab in your Viewport 2D node.
If your topmost render pass can have all your other render passes as its children, you do not need a Group render pass.
![../../_images/group-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/group-render-pass.svg)
###  Material Setup render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#material-setup-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Material Setup render pass allows you to set properties for a material so that all successive rendering with that material uses the property values that you set in this render pass.
See [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html).
![../../_images/material-setup-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-setup-render-pass.svg)![../../_images/preview-infinity-mirror-completed.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-infinity-mirror-completed.png)
###  Node List render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#node-list-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Node List render pass allows you to filter and hold a list of nodes that you want to render using other render passes.
See [Collecting nodes for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/filtering-node-lists.html).
![../../_images/node-list-render-pass1.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-list-render-pass1.svg)
###  Pipeline State render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#pipeline-state-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Pipeline State render pass allows you to set for its child render passes depth and stencil testing, transparency, and culling. This render pass sets the rendering state before passing the control to its descendants. After the descendant render passes of a Pipeline State render pass execute, Kanzi restores the rendering state. See [Setting the cull mode](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/meshes/setting-culling.html#setting-the-cull-mode), [Applying a stencil to 3D content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/stencil-buffer.html), and [Rendering decals](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-decals.html).
![../../_images/pipeline-state-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/pipeline-state-render-pass.svg)
## Render Pass Presets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#render-pass-presets "Link to this heading")
###  Compose and Blit Pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#compose-and-blit-pass "Link to this heading")
Compose and Blit Pass contains the render pass structure that enables you to blit to the screen Composition Target render passes or textures using a specific material.
See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html).
![../../_images/compose-and-blit-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/compose-and-blit-pass.svg)
###  Default render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#default-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Default render pass contains a basic set of render passes that first render opaque nodes and then transparent nodes.
Use the Default render pass as a starting point for your render pass tree. See [Using the Default render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#using-drp).
![../../_images/default-render-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/default-render-pass.svg)
###  Render to Texture Pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#render-to-texture-pass "Link to this heading")
Render to Texture Pass creates the render passes and texture you need to render to a texture.
See [Rendering to texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#rendering-to-texture).
![../../_images/render-to-texture-pass.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-to-texture-pass.svg)
###  Image-Based Lighting Filter Pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#image-based-lighting-filter-pass "Link to this heading")
Image-Based Lighting Filter Pass contains the render passes that enable you to create dynamic Environment Ambient Texture and Environment Reflection Texture cubemap textures for real-time image-based lighting. See [Rendering cubemaps for dynamic image-based lighting](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#rendering-cubemaps-for-dynamic-image-based-lighting).
![../../_images/render-passes-image-based-lighting.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-passes-image-based-lighting.svg)![../../_images/rendering-cubemaps-dynamic-ibl.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rendering-cubemaps-dynamic-ibl.gif)

sub_documents.title: Using resource files
sub_documents.summary: This page explains how Kanzi Studio manages resource files in a Kanzi project. It describes the resource directories (3D Assets, Images, Generic, Fonts, Shaders) that appear in the Library > Resource Files, how to add and remove resource files, and notes that resource files are part of the application but do not consume CPU/GPU resources until instantiated. It also clarifies that adding assets to Resource Files does not make them available as project assets; they must be imported separately.

# Using resource files[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resource-files/resource-files.html#using-resource-files "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Kanzi Studio lists in the Library > Resource Files references to files in the resource directories of a Kanzi project. Kanzi Studio synchronizes the content of Resource Files with the files in the resource directories.
In projects that you create using the Kanzi Studio project template, the resource directories are located in the `<KanziWorkspace>/Projects/<ProjectName>` directory. In projects that you create using other templates, they are located in the `<KanziWorkspace>/Projects/<ProjectName>/Tool_project` directory.
Whenever you modify the files in a resource directory, Kanzi Studio updates them in your project.
Resource files are part of a Kanzi application, but do not consume CPU or GPU resources until you instantiate them.
In Kanzi Studio, the Library > Resource Files contains these directories:
  * 3D Assets. Kanzi Studio stores the 3D assets that you import to your project in `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/3D Assets`. See [Importing 3D assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/3d-assets/importing-3d-assets.html).
  * Images. Kanzi Studio stores image files that you import to your project in `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Images`. See [Importing images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-images.html).
  * Generic. Kanzi Studio stores the files that you add to the Resource Files and that Kanzi Studio does not recognize as either a 3D asset, image, font, or shader, in `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Generic`.
Kanzi Studio does not process the resources in this directory, but exports them to the kzb file.
For example, if your project uses plugins that extend Kanzi to handle new file formats or data types, you can place such files in the Generic directory. This way you can load files from a kzb file instead of the target device file system.
  * Fonts. Kanzi Studio stores font files that you import to your project in `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Fonts`. See [Importing fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html).
  * Shaders. Kanzi Studio stores shader files that you create in your project or add to the Resource Files in `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Shaders`. See [Shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/shaders.html).

![../../_images/resource-files.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resource-files.png)
## Adding resource files to a Kanzi Studio project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resource-files/resource-files.html#adding-resource-files-to-a-ks-project "Link to this heading")
To add resource files to a Kanzi Studio project:
  * Drag files from File Explorer to the Library > Resource Files.
Kanzi Studio copies the files to the resource directory that corresponds to the type of each file.
For example, Kanzi Studio copies PNG image files to `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Images` or `<ProjectName>/Images`.
  * In File Explorer, copy files to the resource directories of a Kanzi Studio project.
Kanzi Studio shows the files in the Library > Resource Files.


When you add 3D assets, images, and fonts to the Resource Files, they are not available as project assets in Kanzi Studio. To make them available as project assets, import the assets to the project. See [Importing](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing.html).
## Removing resource files from a Kanzi Studio project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resource-files/resource-files.html#removing-resource-files-from-a-ks-project "Link to this heading")
When you remove files from a project resource directory, Kanzi Studio keeps in the Resource Files the reference to the removed files. This way you can replace the removed files in the project without losing references to those files.
To remove a resource file from a Kanzi Studio project, in the Library > Resource Files right-click the file and select Delete.
Kanzi Studio removes the file from the Resource Files and deletes it from the project resource directory.

sub_documents.title: Resources
sub_documents.summary: This page from the Kanzi documentation introduces the concept of resources in Kanzi Studio, which are reusable items such as meshes, brushes, and materials. It explains that resources are found in the Library window and the Dictionaries window, and describes various Library views (Animations, Bookmarks, Materials and Textures, Meshes, Property Types, Rendering, Resource Files, State Managers, Textures, Trajectories) that can be enabled to show specific resource types. It also covers loading resources asynchronously for prefabs and using resource profiling to measure loading times. The page provides links to related topics such as resource dictionaries, resource management, bindings, unused resources, and cleaning up projects.

# Resources[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/resources.html#resources "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

In Kanzi, a resource is an item that you can reuse in different parts of your application. For example, a Mesh Data resource defines the geometry of a Model node, and you can use the same Color Brush in different nodes to set the Foreground Brush or Background Brush properties.
You can find all resources in a Kanzi Studio project in the Library window.
![../../_images/resources-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resources-in-library.png)
The Dictionaries window shows the resources in:
  * The resource dictionaries that the node you select in the Node Tree can access. See [Using resource dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/using-resource-dictionaries.html).
  * The localization tables and theme groups in the project. See [Localization](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/localization.html) and [Theming your applications](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html).

![../../_images/resources-in-dictionaries.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resources-in-dictionaries.png)
##  Library views[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/resources.html#library-views "Link to this heading")
By default, the Library shows all the resources in a project. Kanzi Studio provides Library views to show only selected resources in your project. You can enable these views in the Window menu:
  * Animations shows animation data, animation clips, timeline sequences, and timeline entries in your project. See [Animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/animations.html).
  * Bookmarks shows the shortcuts in your project. See [Using bookmarks](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html).
  * Materials and Textures shows brushes, materials, material types, shader formats, and textures in your project. See [Using brushes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html), [Material types and materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/materials.html), [Using binary shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/using-binary-shaders.html), and [Textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html).
  * Meshes shows the mesh data in your project. See [Using meshes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/meshes.html).
  * Property Types shows the custom property types in your project. See [Property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/property-types.html).
  * Rendering shows the object sources, render passes, and filters in your project. See [Using object sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/object-sources/using-object-sources.html), [Rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html), and [Filters](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/filters.html).
  * Resource Files shows the resource files in your project grouped by file type. See [Using resource files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resource-files/resource-files.html).
  * State Managers shows the state managers in your project. See [State manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/state-managers.html).
  * Textures shows the textures in your project. See [Textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html).
  * Trajectories shows the trajectories in your project. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).

![../../_images/window-menu-available-windows.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/window-menu-available-windows.png)
You can add any window as a tab to any other window to see more than one type of content in the same window.
See [Customizing the Kanzi Studio interface](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html).
## Load resources asynchronously[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/resources.html#load-resources-asynchronously "Link to this heading")
In Kanzi, you can load resource dictionaries of prefabs you use in your project before your Kanzi application shows them to users. For example, you can create a loading screen that your users see while Kanzi is loading the resource dictionaries of the rest of your application in the background.
See [Loading node prefab resources asynchronously](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#loading-node-prefab-resources-asynchronously).
Use resource profiling to measure during runtime how long it takes to load and deploy resources and prefabs in your Kanzi application.
Resource profiling data helps you find out which resources to load asynchronously.
See [Measuring the loading and deployment time of resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/performance-profiling/resource-profiling.html).

The Kanzi Rust API provides ready-made, rich, idiomatic bindings to the Kanzi Engine C++ API, enabling you to use the Kanzi Engine in your Rust applications.
This version covers an initial subset of the most commonly used features.
Note
As this is a prerelease of the Kanzi Rust API, some functionality, workflow, and the API is likely to change in future releases.
Your feedback is very important to us. To submit your feedback, use this [feedback form](https://docs.kanzi.com/feedback/v1/forms/feedback-feature.html?featureId=KanziRustAPI&featureTitle=the%20Kanzi%20Rust%20API&productArea=studio).
This topic provides an overview of creating a Rust based project in Kanzi Studio. For detailed steps on configuring your environment for Rust, including Examples and full API reference documentation, see the [Kanzi Rust API](https://docs.kanzi.com/rust/latest-4-0-rust/overview.html) documentation.
## Setting up environment for Kanzi Rust API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rust/using-rust.html#setting-up-environment-for-kzrust "Link to this heading")
Before you can use Kanzi Rust API in your Kanzi application, you must install and configure your environment. See [Setting up environment for Kanzi Rust API](https://docs.kanzi.com/rust/latest-4-0-rust/setting-up.html#setting-up-environment-for-kzrust).
## Create new Rust based project in Kanzi Studio[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rust/using-rust.html#create-new-rust-based-project-in-ks "Link to this heading")
In the Kanzi Studio New Project window:
  1. Set Template to:
     * Application with Rust API to create a Kanzi application with the application logic written in Rust language.
     * Application with Rust plugin to create a Kanzi application with the Kanzi data source plugin written in Rust language.
  2. Click Create.
Kanzi Studio creates a project with the application code boilerplate written in linked extendable C++ and Rust parts.


See how to [Build a Kanzi Rust application](https://docs.kanzi.com/rust/latest-4-0-rust/using-rust-in-application.html#build-a-k-rust-application) or [Build a Kanzi Engine Rust plugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/rust/latest-4-0-rust/using-rust-plugins.html#build-a-kr-rust-plugin).
Kanzi Rust API application templates also come with ready-made Visual Studio Code launch and task configs.
## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rust/using-rust.html#sa "Link to this heading")

sub_documents.title: Using the Scene node
sub_documents.summary: This page explains the Scene node in Kanzi, which is used to display 3D content within a Kanzi application. It describes how to create a Scene node under a Viewport 2D node, notes that a new scene contains a Camera and Directional Light, and mentions that Scene nodes can contain lights, cameras, and other 3D nodes. It also provides API references and links to property types and messages for the Scene node.

# Using the Scene node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scenes/scenes.html#using-the-scene-node "Link to this heading")

Use the Scene node to show 3D content in your Kanzi application.
The Scene node can contain light nodes, Camera node, and all other Kanzi 3D nodes.
Once you import or create content in a scene, move the content around the node tree to place the content where you want it to appear in your Kanzi application. Note that for all inheritable properties (for example, transformation), a change in a parent node affects all its children. See [Property system](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/property-system.html).
## Creating a Scene node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scenes/scenes.html#creating-a-scene-node "Link to this heading")
Only the Viewport 2D node can render a Scene node. However, you can create a Scene node in the Prefabs and instantiate it when you want to show the content of that Scene in your application.
To create a Scene node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the RootNode and select Viewport 2D.
  2. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the Viewport 2D and select Scene.
When you create a new scene it contains only a Camera and a Directional Light.


## Using the Scene node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scenes/scenes.html#using-the-scene-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `Scene[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13894.html)` class.
##  Scene property types and messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scenes/scenes.html#scene-property-types-and-messages "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types and messages for the Scene node, see [Scene](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/scene-reference.html).
