# Text[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#text "Link to this heading") ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg) ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs. ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown View this page as Markdown. ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude Ask Claude about this topic. ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT Ask ChatGPT about this topic. ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code. ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude Download and run the Claude mcpb. Kanzi has these text nodes: * Use the Text Block nodes to show a small amount of text in your application. See [Using the Text Block nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html). ![../../_images/text-blcok-2d-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-blcok-2d-icon.png) * Use the Text Box nodes to add single-line text input to your application. See [Using the Text Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html). ![../../_images/text-box-2d-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-icon.png) ## Font type[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#font-type "Link to this heading") The default font family in Kanzi is [Fira Sans Regular](https://mozilla.github.io/Fira/). The font file is stored in `/Studio/Asset Library/Fonts`. When you want to use your own font, import it to your Kanzi Studio project. See [Importing fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html). You can use these font types in your Kanzi applications: * TrueType and OpenType fonts (ttf and otf files) * iType linked fonts (ltt files). See [iType linked fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#itype-linked-fonts). * Bitmap fonts (fnt files). See [Using bitmap fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#using-bitmap-fonts). Make sure that the font you use includes all the glyphs for the text that you want to include in your Kanzi application. ## Font size[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#font-size "Link to this heading") Kanzi sets the size of fonts in pixels. When you set the Font Size property, Kanzi passes that value to the Freetype library, which Kanzi uses to render fonts, using the [FT_Set_Char_Size](https://www.freetype.org/freetype2/docs/reference/ft2-base_interface.html#FT_Set_Char_Size) function with the default dpi value of 72. For example, both of these display the letter H of the same size: * Text Block or Text Box nodes with these properties set: * Text to H * Font Family to Arial * Font Size to 36 * HTML markup ```

H

``` Copy to clipboard If you want to control the dpi scaling or set the font size in units other than pixels, you must implement that functionality in your Kanzi application. For example, if you want to automatically select the content that the images and layouts in your project use based on the dpi setting, implement that functionality in your Kanzi application. ## Setting the font engine for the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#setting-the-font-engine-for-the-preview "Link to this heading") You can set which font engine you want the Kanzi Studio Preview to use to render the text in your application. To set the font engine for the Preview: 1. In the main menu select Project > Properties. ![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) 2. In the Properties set the Font Engine property: * FreeType uses the FreeType rasterizer, HarfBuzz shaper, and ICU bidirectional library, and libunibreak for line breaking. This is the default font engine. * iType uses the Monotype iType rasterizer and WorldType® Shaper™ for shaping. See [Installing the iType font engine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#installing-the-itype-font-engine). * None to not load a font engine. When you do not load a font engine, the Preview does not render the text in your application. ![../../_images/font-engine.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-engine.png) To learn how to set which font engine to load at application startup, see [FontEngine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#fontengine). ## Setting font hinting[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#setting-font-hinting "Link to this heading") Font hinting provides instructions for rasterization: mapping the outlines of fonts to screen pixels. Font hinting aims to both maintain the design aesthetic of a font and optimize the readability of the font at different sizes. Text nodes in Kanzi by default use the font hinting data included in a font. For example, font hinting can affect the height and width of characters, the width of lines, edge contrast, and the space between characters. To set font hinting for a Text Block or Text Box node, in the Node Tree select that node, in the Properties add the Font Hinting Preference property, and set it to: * No hinting to render text without font hinting. * Native hinting to render text using the hinting data included in the font. If the font does not contain hinting data, Kanzi uses the hinter of the font engine rasterizer. This is the default value. * Auto hinting to render text using the hinter of the font engine rasterizer. See [Setting the font engine for the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#setting-font-engine-for-preview). ![../../_images/font-hinting-preference.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-hinting-preference.png) ## Font fallback[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#font-fallback "Link to this heading") In Kanzi, you can define a Fallback Font Chain for a Font Family. If a character is not available in the current font, Kanzi searches the fallback font chain in order, selecting the first font family that contains the missing character. If the character is not found in any fallback font family, the glyph with **glyph ID 0** in the current font is used as the missing glyph character. Use fallback fonts to: * Display multiple languages in a single text node. * Show special characters like emojis and symbols alongside regular text. When rendering with a fallback font, Kanzi attempts to select a font file from the fallback family that closely matches the style and weight of the current font. To optimize performance and memory usage, fallback fonts are only loaded when a character is not found in the current font or any of the earlier fallback fonts in the chain. To configure the Fallback Font Chain, you can choose from existing font families using the dropdown menu, or add a font family using a kzb URL. ![../../_images/font-fallbacks.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-fallbacks.png) ## Color fonts[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#color-fonts "Link to this heading") To render emoji and other colored glyphs, import a font file that contains color glyphs. The color font file can be either the primary font of a Font Family or a fallback font. These color font formats are supported for each Kanzi font engine: | Font file type | FreeType | iType | | --- | --- | --- | | glyf table (normal non-colored scalable text and icons) | ✅ | ✅ | | CBDT table (non-scalable PNG images) | ✅ | ✅ | | SBIX table (non-scalable PNG images) | ✅ | ❌ | | COLRv0 table (scalable shapes with solid colors) | ✅ | ✅ | | SVG table (SVG images with color gradients) | ❌ | ❌ | | COLRv1 table (scalable shapes with color gradients) | ❌ | ❌ | When you use a font file that contains glyphs in a non-supported font format: * If the font file contains glyphs in multiple formats, Kanzi uses non-colored version of the glyphs * Kanzi does not render the glyphs Note Kanzi renders colored glyphs using a different brush and material than normal text. This material uses only the alpha channel of the Foreground Brush property color (Font Color property for 3D text). This means that you can change the color of text without affecting the emoji colors. ![../../_images/color-fonts.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-fonts.png) ## Customizing word wrapping in Thai text with iType font engine[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#customizing-word-wrapping-in-thai-text-with-itype-font-engine "Link to this heading") You can customize how Kanzi iType font engine wraps words in Thai text by setting a Thai dictionary that you want to use instead of the one that is built into the iType font engine. WorldType® SDK comes with: * Thai dictionary * Python utility that creates a Thai dictionary that your application can use You can find these resources in the WorldType® SDK in the `wtle/product/tools/language_dictionaries/thai` directory. To wrap words automatically in Thai text: 1. Create a Thai dictionary for the iType font engine by passing to `GenerateThaiDictionary.py`: * Thai dictionary in plain-text format * File where you want to store the generated dictionary ``` py -2 GenerateThaiDictionary.py thai-dictionary.txt thai-dictionary.wtd ``` Copy to clipboard `GenerateThaiDictionary.py` creates a wtd file that you set in the application configuration of your Kanzi application: ``` Reading lines from file "thai-dictionary.txt"... done. Extracting, filtering, and normalizing words... done. Adding words to trie... done. number of words: 8 number of characters: 31 longest word length: 7 number of trie nodes: 32 number of trie edges: 31 Compressing trie into a DAWG (Directed Acyclic Word Graph)... done. number of edges in root node: 9 number of DAWG nodes: 24 number of DAWG edges: 30 edges / characters = 96.8 % dawgEdges / trieEdges = 96.0 % dawgNodes / trieNodes = 75.0 % DAWG array elements: 31 Writing DAWG to file "thai-dictionary.wtd"... done. file size: 0 k ``` Copy to clipboard 2. To set your application to use the Thai dictionary that you created, in a text editor set the iType font engine dictionary in the `/Application/bin/application.cfg` file: ``` # Set additional backend dictionaries. ITypeDictionaryUrls = file:///usr/share/itype/thai-dictionary.wtd ``` Copy to clipboard See [Font engine dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#font-engine-dictionaries). 3. (Optional) To set the Kanzi Studio Preview to correctly render Thai text when you use the iType font engine, in Kanzi Studio open your project and in the main menu select Project > Properties. In the Properties set the Preview Working Directory property to the directory that contains the `application.cfg` file that you created in the previous step. ![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/properties-preview-working-directory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-preview-working-directory.png) ## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#sa "Link to this heading") [Using the Text Block nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html) [Using the Text Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html) [Importing fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html) [Glyph cache texture size](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#glyph-cache-texture-size)

sub_documents.title: Textures
sub_documents.summary: This page from the Kanzi framework documentation explains how to use textures in Kanzi Studio and the Kanzi API. It covers texture types (single, cubemap, volume, render target, and cubemap render target), how to create textures from image files, factors affecting loading time (image size, compression, texture compression), and how to set the image target format during kzb export. It also describes properties such as Premultiply Alpha, Generate Mipmaps, Round up Image Dimensions to Nearest Power of Two, Use Original Image, sRGB Content, and Linear Premultiply, and mentions using textures in the API via the Texture class.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html#textures "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use textures to show content in Image nodes, to set the look of textured materials, and to show content in Texture Brush brushes. You can create textures from common image file formats.
See [Images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/images.html).
In a Kanzi Studio project, image files are located in Library > Resource Files > Images. These image files correspond to files on your hard drive. When you modify a file on the hard drive, Kanzi automatically applies the modifications to the textures generated from that file. If you remove the file from the hard drive, you cannot use the file in your Kanzi project.
![../../_images/resource-files-images-defaulttextureimage.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resource-files-images-defaulttextureimage.png)
Loading time of images depends on their size and compression:
  * **Image size** defines the time required to load the data into RAM.
  * **Image compression** can reduce the size, but keep in mind that before your application can use the image, it must decompress it, which is often slower than loading the raw data. You can often achieve the fastest start-up times when using Raw image format, where data is loaded into RAM and sent to the GPU memory. See [Image Compression](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/images.html#image-compression).
  * **Texture compression** you can use on devices with GPUs that support the selected compression algorithm. When using compression, the data size is smaller both when loading from kzb file to RAM and when loading from RAM to the GPU memory. Also less GPU memory is reserved. Depending on the target hardware, by using texture compression you can reduce loading times. Before using texture compression, make sure that your target platform supports the texture compression format you selected.
Kanzi supports ASTC, ETC, and BCn compression formats.
If your target hardware does not support the selected texture compression algorithm, when you run your Kanzi application on your target device, Kanzi prints a warning message to the log. Kanzi paints black the surfaces where you use compressed texture formats that your target hardware does not support.
See [Compressing textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html).


## Texture types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html#texture-types "Link to this heading")
These textures are available in Kanzi:  
|  Single textures use a single image for the texture. See [Using single textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html).  |  ![../../_images/single-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/single-texture.png)  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Cubemap textures combine six square-shaped images into one texture to represent reflections of the environment. Each image represents the scenery in one of the six directions along the x, y, and z axes from the viewpoint of the cubemapped object. See [Using cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-cubemap-textures.html).  |  ![../../_images/cubemap-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cubemap-texture.png)  |  
|  Volume textures use a single 2D image, made up of many cross-section slices of a 3D shape, to define a 3D volume texture. This technique is often used for effects like smoke, fire, or clouds, where 3D data would be too resource intensive or difficult to generate procedurally. See [Using volume textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html).  |  ![../../_images/volume-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/volume-texture.png)  |  
|  Use a Render Target Texture to render content to a texture or to apply anti-aliasing to only a part of your application. You can use render target textures like any other texture. For example, you can use it in a Texture Brush or as an image in an Image node. See [Using render target textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-render-target-textures.html) and [Using OpenGL ES 3.0+ in Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html).  |  ![../../_images/render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-target-texture.png)  |  
|  Use a Cubemap Render Target Texture to render a Cubemap render pass to a cubemap texture. See [Creating cubemap reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/cubemap-render-pass.html).  |  ![../../_images/cubemap-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cubemap-render-target-texture.png)  |  
You can use .exr, .dds, and .hdr images with half float and floating point data to bring HDR images to your Kanzi project. See [Setting the color format of textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html#setting-the-color-format-of-textures).
## Setting the image target format[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html#setting-the-image-target-format "Link to this heading")
When you export your project to a kzb file, Kanzi Studio reads the images in the project using the format of the original image and writes the images to a kzb file in the format you set with the Target Format property for each image.
If the file format of the original image is the same as the format you select in the Target Format property, Kanzi Studio does not modify the image when it writes the image to a kzb file under these conditions:
  * Premultiply Alpha is disabled, or the alpha channel does not need to be premultiplied
To change this setting, in the Project > Properties use the Premultiply Alpha property. You can override this value in the properties of the image file where you want to use a different setting.
![../../_images/premultiply-alpha-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/premultiply-alpha-project.png) ![../../_images/premultiply-alpha-image.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/premultiply-alpha-image.png)
  * Generate Mipmaps is disabled
You can set the value of the Generate Mipmaps property in each image file.
![../../_images/generate-mipmaps-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/generate-mipmaps-disabled.png)
  * Round up Image Dimensions to Nearest Power of Two property is disabled
You can set the value of the Round up Image Dimensions to Nearest Power of Two property in the Project > Properties.
When you enable the Round up Image Dimensions to Nearest Power of Two property, Kanzi Studio rounds up the width and height of the images in your project to the nearest power of two during kzb file export. For example, Kanzi Studio exports an image of the size 40 by 30 pixels to the kzb file in the size 64 by 32 pixels.
![../../_images/round-images-to-nearest-power-of-2-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/round-images-to-nearest-power-of-2-disabled.png)


If your image is in JPEG or PNG format and you do not want Kanzi Studio to modify the image that it exports to a kzb file, in the image Properties enable the Use Original Image property.
![../../_images/use-original-image-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/use-original-image-enabled.png)
To set the image target format:
  1. In the Library > Resource Files > Images select the image for which you want to set the target format.
![../../_images/resource-files-images-defaulttextureimage.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resource-files-images-defaulttextureimage.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Target Format property to the image format you want to use in your Kanzi application.
The format you select is important because this influences the size of the kzb file and the loading time when your Kanzi application loads the image. Make sure that your target device supports the target format you select for the image. See [Images and textures best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/images-and-textures-best-practices.html) and [Compressing textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html).
![../../_images/target-format-astc-compression.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-format-astc-compression.png)
  3. If the image format you selected in the previous step supports compression, configure the compression scheme you want to use. See [Compressing textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html).
![../../_images/astc-block-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/astc-block-size.png)
  4. For image formats that support sRGB:
     * If the image contains sRGB color information, set the sRGB Content property to enabled. This is the default setting.
If you disable the sRGB Content property for an image that contains sRGB color information, Kanzi can render the textures that use the image brighter than expected.
     * If the image contains non-color information, such as a normal, roughness, or occlusion map, set the sRGB Content property to disabled.
Textures that contain non-color information are stored in linear format. By disabling the sRGB Content property you set Kanzi to pass the image data to a shader directly, without performing a color space conversion.
![../../_images/srgb-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/srgb-content.png)
  5. If you want Kanzi to premultiply the alpha channel in the:
     * Linear color space, set the Linear Premultiply property to enabled.
This is the default value and results in the fewest artifacts in sRGB images.
     * Color space of the image, usually sRGB, set the Linear Premultiply property to disabled.
This can give better results for images created for the standard color workflow.
See [Preparing images in third-party tools](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/preparing-images-in-3rd-party-tools.html).
![../../_images/linear-premultiply.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linear-premultiply.png)


## Using textures in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html#using-textures-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `Texture[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a12570.html)` class.

sub_documents.summary: This page explains how to theme Kanzi applications using Theme Groups and Themes. It covers creating Theme Groups, adding resources to them, setting resources per Theme in the Theme Editor, using kzb file URLs for resources, and viewing Themes in the Preview. It also mentions exporting themes and provides links to related tutorials and documentation.

# Theming your applications[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#theming-your-applications "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Themes enable you to use a single Kanzi Studio project for multiple variants of your product.
For example, in a single project you can define Kanzi applications for different car models and different visual themes for each car model.
Creating themes for your application involves the creation and use of different resources, such as, text, textures, brushes, materials, and styles, and layouts for themes that you want to use in your applications.
A Theme Group defines a collection of Themes. Each Theme in a Theme Group defines the look and feel of your application. In your Kanzi Studio project you can define more than one Theme Group, where each contains several Themes. In your Kanzi application you can apply one Theme from each Theme Group at a time. For example, you can use one Theme Group to define a car model, such as hatchback, minivan, pickup, sedan, and SUV, and another Theme Group to define the look of the interface for each of the car models, such as, classic, digital, modern, and sport.
Kanzi uses themed resources indirectly using resource IDs that hold a separate value for each Theme. In the Library > Themes you can see all Theme Group items in your Kanzi Studio project.
![../../_images/export-example-library-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-example-library-color.png)
To create a theme for your application:
  1. Create a Theme Group and add to it the resources in your project which you want to define with a Theme. See [Adding resources used in a project to a Theme Group](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#adding-resources-used-in-project-to-theme-group).
  2. Create and import resources each Theme uses. See [Setting resources for a Theme](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#setting-resources-for-theme).
  3. View a Theme in the Preview. See [Viewing a theme in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#viewing).
  4. Export resources used by a Theme to kzb files. See [Exporting Themes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/exporting-themes.html).


Learn how to theme your Kanzi applications by completing a tutorial. See [Tutorial: Theme your application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/theming/theming.html).
## Adding resources used in a project to a Theme Group[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#adding-resources-used-in-a-project-to-a-theme-group "Link to this heading")
Start creating a theme for your Kanzi application by adding resources which you want to theme to a Theme Group. The easiest way to add resources to a Theme Group is to use the Add Resources to a Theme Group command on a node in the Node Tree.
When you use the Add Resources to a Theme Group command in the Node Tree, Kanzi Studio automatically creates a resource ID for each resource in the node and nodes in its tree and sets each node to use those resource IDs.
To add resources used in a project to a Theme Group:
  1. In the Node Tree right-click the Screen node and in the context menu select Add Resources to a Theme Group.
When you use the Add Resources to a Theme Group command on the Screen node, Kanzi Studio enables you to add all resources in your project to a Theme Group and change their appearance in each Theme. To add to a Theme Group resources only from a selected node or prefab and its tree, right-click that node or prefab and select Add Resources to a Theme Group.
![../../_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png)
  2. In the Add Resources to a Theme Group window set:
    1. Theme Group to the Theme Group to which you want to add the resources. If you do not have a Theme Group yet, select <Create New>.
A Theme Group defines a collection of Themes.
    2. Select the resource type you want to show in the Add Resources to a Theme Group window.
For example, to show only text and image resources select ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resource-type-text.png) and ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resource-type-image.png).
![../../_images/show-resource-types.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/show-resource-types.png)
    3. In the table that lists all resources of the types you selected, click the checkbox next to the resource you want to add to the Theme Group you selected. To change the resource ID, double-click the resource ID and enter a new name.
Kanzi Studio creates a single resource ID for Text Block nodes which use the same value for the Text property. These nodes share the same entry in a Theme Group.
    4. Click Add.
Kanzi Studio creates resource IDs from all resources and adds them to the Theme Group you selected. You can find Theme Group items in the Library > Themes. In the Theme Group you can now create Themes and set which resource you want to use for which Theme. See [Setting resources for a Theme](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#setting-resources-for-theme).
![../../_images/library-themes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-themes.png)


## Setting resources for a Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#setting-resources-for-a-theme "Link to this heading")
After you add resources used in your project to a Theme Group you can create a Theme and define the resources used by each Theme.
To set resources for a Theme:
  1. Create and import resources you want to use for each Theme. For example:
     * In the Library create the resources, such as, brushes, styles, and materials which set the appearance for each theme in your application.
     * In the Prefabs create the layouts which arrange the UI elements for each theme in your application.
     * In the Assets import the 2D and 3D assets which you want to use in a Theme.
  2. In the Library > Themes double-click the Theme Group where you want to define a Theme.
  3. In the Theme Editor click Create Theme and name the Theme.
![../../_images/create-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-theme.png)
  4. In the column of the theme you created in the previous step, double-click the cell for each resource, and set the resource you want to use for the resource ID in that row.
     * If you do not select a resource or value for a Theme, Kanzi uses the default resource or value for that Theme. The default value is listed in the Default Value column.
Black cells mark entries which use the default value.
     * To use an empty string for a text resource, enter a value, delete the value, and then press the `Enter` key.
Gray cells mark entries which use an empty string.
     * To use a resource from the file system, in the cell for which you want to set the resource select < URL >, and enter `file://` followed by the absolute or relative path to the resource in the file system.
![../../_images/theme-editor-set-resource.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/theme-editor-set-resource.png)


## Using a kzb file URL for a resource in a Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#using-a-kzb-file-url-for-a-resource-in-a-theme "Link to this heading")
After you add resources used in your project to a Theme Group, you can use a kzb file URL to point to a resource in another Kanzi Studio project.
To use a kzb file URL for a resource in a Theme:
  1. In the Library > Themes double-click the Theme Group where you want to define a Theme.
  2. In the Theme Editor click Create Theme and name the Theme.
![../../_images/create-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-theme.png)
  3. In the column of the Theme you created in the previous step, double-click the cell for the resource for which you want to use a kzb file URL, and in the dropdown menu select < URL >.
![../../_images/select-url-in-theme-editor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-url-in-theme-editor.png)
  4. In the cell enter the kzb file URL of the resource you want to use.
For example, to use a font from another Kanzi Studio project, enter the kzb file URL pointing to that font.
![../../_images/set-kzb-url-in-theme-editor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-kzb-url-in-theme-editor.png)


## Viewing a theme in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#viewing-a-theme-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
When you are defining a Theme for your application, you can set the Preview to show that Theme without adding to the application a control for switching Themes.
To view a Theme in the Preview:
  * In the Dictionaries click Locales and Themes to enable the viewing of Localization Table and Theme Group items, and for each Theme Group select the Theme you want to see in the Preview.
![../../_images/activate-theme-dictionaries.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/activate-theme-dictionaries.png)
  * In the Library select the Theme Group which contains the Theme you want to view and in the Properties set the Selected Theme property to that Theme.
![../../_images/export-example-library-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-example-library-color.png) ![../../_images/properties-startup-theme.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-startup-theme.png)


## See also[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#sa "Link to this heading")
[Tutorial: Theme your application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/theming/theming.html)
[Exporting Themes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/exporting-themes.html)
[Using Themes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html)

sub_documents.title: Trajectories
sub_documents.summary: This page introduces trajectories in Kanzi Studio, which are 3D paths used by Trajectory Layout 3D/2D nodes and Trajectory List Box 3D nodes to arrange or move child nodes/items. It lists the available trajectory types (Angle, Arc, Circle, Ellipse, Line, Rectangle, Spiral, Spline, Trapezoid) with links to detailed usage pages, and mentions the Trajectory API class for programmatic use.

# Trajectories[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html#trajectories "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
Trajectories are paths in 3D space. See [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html) and [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html).
Kanzi Studio comes with these trajectory types:
  * Use an Angle Trajectory to create a path where two straight lines form an angle in 3D space.
See [Using angle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-angle-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/angle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/angle.png)
  * Use an Arc Trajectory to create a path in the shape of an arc in 3D space.
See [Using arc trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-arc-trajectories.html)
![../../_images/arc.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/arc.png)
  * Use a Circle Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a circle in 3D space.
See [Using circle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-circle-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/circle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/circle.png)
  * Use an Ellipse Trajectory to create a path in the shape of an ellipse in 3D space.
See [Using ellipse trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-ellipse-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/ellipse.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ellipse.png)
  * Use a Line Trajectory to create a path with a single straight line in 3D space.
See [Using line trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-line-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/line.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/line.png)
  * Use a Rectangle Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a rectangle in 3D space.
See [Using rectangle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-rectangle-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/rectangle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rectangle.png)
  * Use a Spiral Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a spiral in 3D space.
See [Using spiral trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spiral-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/spiral.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/spiral.png)
  * Use a Spline Trajectory to import a trajectory defined by a set of points and control points in 3D space you created in a third-party tool.
See [Using spline trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html).
  * Use a Trapezoid Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a trapezoid in 3D space.
See [Using trapezoid trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trapezoid-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/trapezoid.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trapezoid.png)


## Using trajectories in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html#using-trajectories-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `Trajectory[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a14098.html)` class.

sub_documents.title: Using the Trajectory Layout nodes
sub_documents.summary: This page explains how to use Trajectory Layout nodes in Kanzi Studio to arrange items along a trajectory path. It covers creating 2D and 3D Trajectory Layout nodes, adding child nodes, selecting different trajectory types (circle, angle, arc, ellipse, line, rectangle, spiral, spline, trapezoid), stretching the trajectory to fill the layout, adjusting distance between items, adjusting start offset, setting appearance of 2D nodes, and using the Trajectory Layout node in the API with code examples. It also lists related property types, messages, and links to further documentation.

# Using the Trajectory Layout nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#using-the-trajectory-layout-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Trajectory Layout nodes to arrange items along a trajectory path.
Kanzi Studio comes with several types of trajectories. When you need a different type of trajectory, create a spline trajectory in a third-party tool and import it to your Kanzi Studio project. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
![../../_images/trajectory-layout.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout.gif)
## Creating a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#creating-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Trajectory Layout node and select either Trajectory Layout 3D, or Trajectory Layout 2D.
![../../_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png)
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
Tip
To see the trajectory, in the Preview click ![image-analyze-off](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode, right-click ![image-analyze-on](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Debug objects.
![../../_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Trajectory Layout 3D node, add several Sphere nodes. If you created a Trajectory Layout 2D node, add several Image nodes.
![../../_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png)
As you add child nodes, the Trajectory Layout node positions them along the trajectory used by the Trajectory Layout node.
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif)
  3. (Optional)
Kanzi Studio creates and uses a circle trajectory by default. You can use an angle, arc, circle, ellipse, line, rectangle, spiral, spline, or a trapezoid trajectory. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif)


## Stretching the trajectory to fill the layout[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#stretching-the-trajectory-to-fill-the-layout "Link to this heading")
By default, the size of the trajectory used by a Trajectory Layout node determines the amount of space that the trajectory occupies in the layout. For example, in a Circle Trajectory, the Radius property determines the size of the trajectory.
To stretch the trajectory to fill the layout:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and enable the Trajectory Layout > Stretch property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif)
## Adjusting the distance between items in a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#adjusting-the-distance-between-items-in-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
A Trajectory Layout node automatically calculates the distance between its child nodes.
To adjust the distance between the child nodes in a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Override Distance property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif)
## Adjusting the position of items in a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#adjusting-the-position-of-items-in-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
By default, a Trajectory Layout node arranges its child nodes from the start of the trajectory spline.
To adjust the starting position of the Trajectory Layout node child nodes on the trajectory:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Start Offset property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif)
## Setting the appearance of a Trajectory Layout 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#setting-the-appearance-of-a-trajectory-layout-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)


## Using the Trajectory Layout node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#using-the-trajectory-layout-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To create a Trajectory Layout 3D node:

```
// Create a Trajectory Layout 3D named Trajectory.
TrajectoryLayout3DSharedPtr trajectoryLayout = TrajectoryLayout3D::create(domain, "Trajectory");

```
Copy to clipboard
To create a trajectory and use it in the Trajectory Layout 3D node:

```
// Create a circle trajectory named Circle with radius of 4 device independent units.
// Set the trajectory layout to use it.
TrajectorySharedPtr trajectory = Trajectory::createCircle(Vector3(), Vector3::positiveY(), 0.0f, 4.0f, domain, "Circle");
trajectoryLayout->setTrajectory(trajectory);

```
Copy to clipboard
To add items to the Trajectory Layout 3D node:

```
// Create cube meshes and add them as items of the trajectory layout.
// Items on the trajectory appear in the order you add them to the trajectory layout.
Model3DSharedPtr item1 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item1", 1.0f, ThemeRed);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item1);
Model3DSharedPtr item2 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item2", 1.0f, ThemeGreen);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item2);
Model3DSharedPtr item3 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item3", 1.0f, ThemeBlue);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item3);
Model3DSharedPtr item4 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item4", 1.0f, ThemeOrange);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item4);
Model3DSharedPtr item5 = Model3D::createCube(domain, "item5", 1.0f, ThemeGray);
trajectoryLayout->addChild(item5);

```
Copy to clipboard
To manually position items in the Trajectory Layout 3D node:

```
// Position an item in the middle of the trajectory.
TrajectoryLayout3D::setOverrideOffset(*item2, 0.5f);

// Set the distance between the items to one third of the length of the trajectory.
trajectoryLayout->setOverrideDistance(0.3f);

```
Copy to clipboard

sub_documents.title: Triggers
sub_documents.summary: This page introduces the Kanzi framework's event-driven logic system, explaining how triggers and actions create interactions. It covers the relationship between input/hit testing, input manipulators, messages (tunneling/bubbling), triggers, and actions. It describes how triggers react to messages or data changes and apply actions like Set Property or Go to State, and mentions that triggers can have settings and conditions. The page also provides links to related documentation on using triggers, messages, input handling, and references for triggers and actions.
sub_documents.markdown_content:
# Triggers[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/triggers.html#triggers "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use triggers and actions to create interactions. Use triggers to set off actions, such as setting a property to a certain value or setting the state of an application.
For example, Kanzi generates messages from user input and these messages are handled by nodes according to specified behavior.
Nodes define most of the message handling behavior, such as scrolling in a List Box node. However, to meet the requirements of your application, you can define additional behavior. For example, a Button node sends a click message when a user clicks that button, but you can define what happens after the sent click message. An example action is that a click triggers an animation that highlights the button that the user clicked.
All Kanzi nodes can send and receive messages and you can intercept these messages with triggers. Some nodes by default receive messages from specific user input events. For example, a Button node by default receives click messages and a Scroll View node by default receives scroll messages.
![../../_images/messages-and-triggers.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/messages-and-triggers.svg)
In Kanzi these concepts relate to defining event-driven logic:
  * **Input and hit testing.** Input is first recognized in a hit testing phase, where all nodes that have Hit Testable property enabled participate. If a pointer event (for example, mouse button down) is performed on top of nodes that participate in hit testing, only the topmost component receives the input. If a node has a manipulator that reacts to the received type of input, it can send messages (for example, a click message). See [Defining which node receives input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#defining-which-node-receives-input), [Using input manipulators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
  * **Input manipulators.** An input manipulator reacts to a specific type of input gesture, such as pan, click, or long press. In Kanzi Studio you can use nodes that already contain specific types of manipulators, or you can add input manipulators using the Kanzi Engine API. For example, a Scroll View node contains a pan manipulator and a Button node includes a click manipulator. See [Using input manipulators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators).
  * **Messages.** Nodes use messages to communicate. The messages travel between nodes using a process called tunneling and bubbling. The message reaches its target node during tunneling and during bubbling messages travel to ancestor nodes, until a trigger intercepts the message and sets it as handled. This enables you to place triggers in nodes themselves, or their ancestors. For example, you can place a trigger called radioButtonHandler to the parent of multiple buttons. See [Using messages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html).
  * **Triggers.** Triggers react to messages, a change in data, or events and apply logic. Kanzi includes the most common action types, such as Set Property or Go to State, but you can use the Kanzi Engine API to define to which messages triggers react. Each trigger includes settings, such as the Set Message Handled property, which prevents the message from bubbling up to other triggers, and conditions which you can use to define conditions under which the trigger sets off. You can add multiple triggers to a single message or event and each can have specific settings and conditions. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html) and [Triggers reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-triggers.html).
  * **Actions.** An action is an outcome of a trigger. Kanzi includes general actions like Set Property, Write Log, Activate Theme, and actions you can use to control a specific type of item such as, Go to State, Set Scroll Target, or Activate Activity. See [Actions and messages reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-actions.html).

sub_documents.title: Using version control systems with Kanzi
sub_documents.summary: This page explains how to use version control systems with Kanzi Studio projects. It lists files and directories that should be excluded from version control (e.g., .kzproj_N, .proj.kzm_N, .lock, .autosave, .user, assets, build_vs2022, compressed, cubemaps, gen, mipmaps, output, lib, thumbnails) and notes that cubemaps and mipmaps are regenerated from source HDR/EXR images, which should be versioned. It describes the Kanzi merge tool for merging .kzproj files, the required parameters (MINE, THEIRS, BASE, MERGED), and provides integration instructions for version control tools, including a specific example for TortoiseSVN.

# Using version control systems with Kanzi[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html#using-version-control-systems-with-k "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
When you add your Kanzi projects to a version control system, do not add these files and directories:
  * `.kzproj_N`
  * `.proj.kzm_N`
  * `.lock`
  * `.autosave`
  * `.user`
  * `assets`
  * `build_vs2022`
  * `compressed`
  * `cubemaps`
  * `gen`
  * `mipmaps`
  * `output`
  * `lib`
  * `thumbnails`


Note
The `cubemaps` and `mipmaps` directories excluded above hold the generated faces and roughness mipmaps of image-based lighting cubemap textures. Kanzi Studio regenerates them from the source image when they are missing, such as after a fresh clone. Therefore, also add to version control the source hdr or exr image from which you created each image-based lighting cubemap texture. See [Using image-based lighting cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html).
## Merging projects using version control tools[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html#merging-projects-using-version-control-tools "Link to this heading")
After configuring your version control tool you can use the Kanzi merge tool for Kanzi project updating and merging. For the integration Kanzi requires a version control tool that provides the necessary parameters to the Kanzi merge tool.  
| Example of parameter types  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| MINE  | The parameter for the source project.  |  
| THEIRS  | The parameter for the target project.  |  
| BASE  | The parameter for the base project.  |  
| MERGED  | The parameter for the merged project.  |  
## Integrating the Kanzi merge tool with a version control tool[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html#integrating-the-k-merge-tool-with-a-version-control-tool "Link to this heading")
To integrate the Kanzi merge tool with a version control tool:
  1. Configure your version control tool to use the Kanzi merge tool (`<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/KanziMergeTool.bat`) for .kzproj files.
  2. Pass to your version control tool the absolute path to the `KanziStudio.exe`. For example, `C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi\Studio\Bin\KanziStudio.exe`.
  3. Set the version control tool parameters for the Kanzi merge tool. For example, these parameters can be called MINE, THEIRS, BASE, MERGED.


## Integrating the Kanzi merge tool with SVN version control software[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html#integrating-the-k-merge-tool-with-svn-version-control-software "Link to this heading")
To integrate the Kanzi merge tool with SVN version control software, add Kanzi merge tool as an external program for merging files with the .kzproj extension.
For example, if you are using Tortoise SVN, in TortoiseSVN select SVN > Settings > External Programs > Merge Tool > Advanced and set:
  * Filename, extension or mime-type to .kzproj
  * External program to

```
<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/KanziMergeTool.bat "<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/KanziStudio.exe"  %mine %theirs %base %merged

```
Copy to clipboard
For example, if your installation of Kanzi is in `C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi`, use

```
C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi\Studio\Bin\KanziMergeTool.bat "C:\Program Files\Rightware\Kanzi\Studio\Bin\KanziStudio.exe" %mine %theirs %base %merged

```
Copy to clipboard

You can customize the Kanzi Studio interface. You can open new, rearrange, dock, and close windows to make the environment that best suits your needs.
To restore the workspace to the default state, in the main menu select Window > Reset Workspace.
![../../_images/reset-workspace.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reset-workspace.png)
This is how Kanzi Studio looks when you create a new project.
![../../_images/interface-overview.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interface-overview.svg)
## Opening windows[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html#opening-windows "Link to this heading")
To open a new window select Window and select the window that you want to open:
  * Use the Activity Browser to create and inspect Activities and Activity Hosts, and to simulate the activation of Activities. The Activity Browser shows all possible UI states of Activities in your application.
See [Using the Activity Browser](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/activity-browser.html).
  * Animations shows animation data, animation clips, timeline sequences, and timeline entries in your project. See [Animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/animations.html).
  * Asset Packages shows collections of ready-made content that you can import to your Kanzi Studio project. See [Asset packages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html).
  * Assets shows the 2D and 3D content, materials, and prefabs in your project.
  * Bookmarks shows the shortcuts in your project. See [Using bookmarks](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html).
  * Data Sources shows the data sources in your project. See [Data sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/data-sources.html).
  * Dictionaries shows the resource IDs of the resources that are local to the node that you select in the Node Tree.
See [Resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/resources.html).
  * Library shows all the resources in your project. Here you can find, create, and edit all the materials, textures, animations, trajectories, composers, and other resources in your project. You can open a separate dockable window for each resource type. See [Resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/resources.html).
  * Log shows the status of your project such as messages triggered in your project, but also warning and error messages.
  * Materials and Textures shows brushes, materials, material types, shader formats, and textures in your project. See [Using brushes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html), [Material types and materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/materials.html), [Using binary shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/using-binary-shaders.html), and [Textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html).
  * Meshes shows the mesh data in your project. See [Using meshes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/meshes.html).
  * Node Components shows the components, such as triggers, animation players, and input manipulators, for the node selected in the Node Tree. See [Node components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/node-components/node-components.html).
  * Node Tree shows all nodes in your project that Kanzi loads at application startup. This is where you create and organize the content of your project.
  * Pages shows the pages tool where you can create and manage the structure of your application. See [Using the Page and Page Host nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/pages/using-pages.html).
  * Prefabs shows the prefabs in your project. See [Using node prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html).
  * Preview shows your project the way it appears to your users. The Preview window has these modes:
    * In the Analyze mode you can analyze the performance and inner structure of your application. See [Analyzing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html).
    * In the Edit mode you can use the Preview window to edit the content in your project. Select any of the Preview window tools ![preview-node-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png) ![grid-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-tool.png) ![text-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-tool.png) ![image3](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-2d-tool.png) ![image4](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-2d-tool.png) ![image5](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/camera-tool.png) to enter the Edit mode.
See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html).
    * In the Interact mode, you can interact with your application in the Preview window as you would on a device. When you are using a Preview tool, to switch to the Interact mode, in the Preview window click ![interact](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interact.png).
  * Prism Editor shows the Prism Editor where you can create and edit Prism effects. See [Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html).
  * Properties shows the properties for the item selected in the Node Tree or Library. When you add, remove, or edit the properties, you edit the look and behavior of the selected item.
  * Property Types shows the custom property types in your project. See [Property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/property-types.html).
  * Rendering shows the object sources, render passes, and filters in your project. See [Using object sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/object-sources/using-object-sources.html), [Rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html), and [Filters](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/filters.html).
  * Resource Files shows the resource files in your project grouped by file type. See [Using resource files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resource-files/resource-files.html).
  * State Managers shows the state managers in your project. See [State manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/state-managers.html).
  * State Tools shows the tools you can use to create, set, and manage states in your application. See [State manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/state-managers.html).
  * Textures shows the textures in your project. See [Textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html).
  * Trajectories shows the trajectories in your project. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).


Tip
To expand or collapse all elements under an item in any tree view, click the expander ![expander](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/expander.png) while holding down `Ctrl`.
## Rearranging windows in your workspace[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html#rearranging-windows-in-your-workspace "Link to this heading")
You can rearrange your workspace by docking, undocking, opening and closing windows.
To undock click the header of the window and drag it either to a new location in the guide diamond, or drop it to keep the window floating.
To close a window, click the X in the header of the window you want to close.
To dock a window:
  1. Click the header of the window you want to dock.
A guide diamond appears in the center of the area where the window is.
![../../_images/click-header-of-a-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-header-of-a-window.png)
  2. Drag the window over the area where you want to dock it, and move it over the corresponding portion of the guide diamond.
The area where the window docks becomes shaded.
![../../_images/shaded-area.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shaded-area.png)
  3. Release the mouse button to dock the window in the indicated position.
![../../_images/docked-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/docked-window.png)


## Adding any window as a tab to another window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html#adding-any-window-as-a-tab-to-another-window "Link to this heading")
You can add any window as a tab to any other window to see more than one type of content in the same window.
To add any window as a tab to another window:
  1. Click and drag the header of the window over the window where you want to add it as a tab, and move it over the central part of the guide diamond.
![../../_images/docking-as-tab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/docking-as-tab.png)
  2. Release the mouse button to add the window as a tab.
![../../_images/docked-tab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/docked-tab.png)


## Ordering property categories in the Properties window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/workspaces/customizing-your-workspace.html#ordering-property-categories-in-the-properties-window "Link to this heading")
To set the order of property categories in the Properties window, select Edit > User Preferences, in the Properties tab in the Property Category dropdown select a property category, and set the position of the property category.
For example, you can set the Transform 2D and your own My Property Category categories to be shown after the Description category.
Note
The General and Description property categories are always shown on the top.
![../../_images/user-preferences-property-category-order.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/user-preferences-property-category-order.png) ![../../_images/properties-property-category-order.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-property-category-order.png)

# Best practices[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#best-practices "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
When creating applications for embedded and mobile devices, even seemingly small details can have significant impact on the performance of your Kanzi application on target devices. Kanzi graphics pipeline is optimized to allow 60 frames per second for 3D instrument clusters and human-machine interfaces. Use the best practices covered in this section of documentation to create optimal Kanzi applications for your target hardware.
Even though Kanzi provides many ways that enable you to create applications that consume less memory, CPU and GPU capacity, and device battery, how you create your application has a large impact on its efficiency.
## Thread safety[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#thread-safety "Link to this heading")
Kanzi is thread-agnostic and does not guarantee thread safety. To make your Kanzi application code thread-safe:
  * Do not call Kanzi functions from custom threads unless the API documentation specifies that you can call the function from any thread.
  * Synchronize between threads all access to shared data.


## Pay attention to the log messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#pay-attention-to-the-log-messages "Link to this heading")
Kanzi prints warnings and errors to the Kanzi Studio Log window and the Kanzi debug console to help you find the problems and bottlenecks in your Kanzi application. Pay careful attention to these messages. To ensure that your Kanzi application works correctly and performs optimally on your target platform, resolve all the issues shown in the warnings and errors. Even seemingly unimportant warnings can have a significant impact on the loading times and performance of your Kanzi application. For example, see [Adjusting the data size](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/adjusting-the-data-size.html).
## Use the Kanzi Command Prompt[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#use-the-kanzi-command-prompt "Link to this heading")
The Kanzi Command Prompt opens the Windows Command Prompt with the Kanzi environment variables set for the version of Kanzi for which you open a Kanzi Command Prompt.
Use the Kanzi Command Prompt to access Kanzi utilities and build tools, such as Gradle and CMake, without using absolute paths or setting environment variables.
See [Using the Kanzi Command Prompt](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/using-kanzi-command-prompt.html).
## Kanzi best practices[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/best-practices.html#k-best-practices "Link to this heading")
Here you can find the information about best practices when working with Kanzi.

sub_documents.summary: This page provides best practices for optimizing the startup time of Kanzi applications. Key recommendations include using raw and compressed image formats instead of PNG/JPG, enabling parallel resource loading, loading a minimal kzb file first (e.g., loading screen) before loading the rest, reorganizing the node tree to postpone resource loading, designing for gradual loading with asynchronous prefab loading, and using the DeploymentQueueBudget setting for Android droidfw applications to control GPU resource deployment time per frame.

# Optimizing the startup time of your application[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/start-up-time.html#optimizing-the-startup-time-of-your-application "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
To optimize the startup time of your Kanzi application:
  * For images in your applications use raw and compressed formats, instead of .png and .jpg formats. When you use raw and compressed formats Kanzi needs to process less data before it sends it to the GPU. See [Images and textures best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/images-and-textures-best-practices.html).
  * Use the parallel resource loading to load and process the resources from your application in multiple threads and deploy the resources to the GPU over multiple frames. See [Loading resources in parallel](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/loading-resources-in-parallel.html).
  * Load first a kzb file which contains the smallest amount of content you can show at application startup, such as a loading screen. Then start loading the kzb files which contain the rest of your application. See [Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html).
  * Reorganize the node tree of your application in Kanzi Studio. Kanzi loads the resources when it needs them. Reorganize the node tree to postpone the loading of resources until less important parts of the node tree become visible. Doing so the application can skip those resources and start faster.
  * Design your application to support gradual loading. For example, show the loading screen while you load the base UI, and once the base UI is loaded and operational, preload the application resources for the other parts of the UI. See [Loading node prefab resources asynchronously](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#loading-node-prefab-resources-asynchronously).
  * For your Kanzi Android framework (droidfw) application, use the `DeploymentQueueBudget` configuration setting to control the amount of time that Kanzi spends each frame to deploy resources. This setting can have a large effect on the startup time. See [DeploymentQueueBudget](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#deploymentqueuebudget).

# Animations best practices[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/animations/animations-best-practices.html#animations-best-practices "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
To create more efficient animations:
  * Remove the keyframes that do not affect the precision of an animation. See [Removing redundant keyframes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/animations/removing-redundant-keyframes.html).
  * Remove the Animation Data channels that do not animate anything.
See [Removing redundant Animation Data channels](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/animations/removing-redundant-animation-data-channels.html).
  * Avoid excessive use of bezier interpolation between keyframes, because bezier interpolation is more expensive than linear, step, and smooth step interpolation.
  * After you import an animation that is heavily sampled, check whether the keyframes are using Bezier interpolation. To significantly reduce the CPU workload, select all keyframes and use linear interpolation. This rarely has an impact on the visual quality of the animation. See [Setting the easing function between keyframes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/animating-property-values.html#setting-the-easing-function-between-keyframes).
  * To dynamically change the size of text in a Text Block node, use the Scale property field of either Render Transformation or Layout Transformation properties, instead of the Font Size property. For example, use this approach when you want to animate the size of text in a Text Block node. When you use the Font Size property to dynamically scale the text, Kanzi creates multiple textures for different font sizes and does not release them from the memory.


Tip
In the Kanzi Studio Node Tree window, an indicator next to a node shows when a State Manager, Binding, Data Source Binding, or an Animation overrides the values of some properties in that node.
![../../_images/node-override-notice.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-override-notice.png)
To navigate to the source of the override in the Kanzi Studio project, right-click the override indicator and select the source you wish to navigate to from the context menu.
